controls.name: Trane IntelliPak UCM module controls with Human Interface (legacy)
controls.description: Module-based control on IntelliPak I rooftops (20-130 t) before Symbio 800: RoofTop Module (RTM, 1U48), Heat module, compressor modules, VAV/exhaust modules and the unit-mounted Human Interface (HI, 1U65) LCD keypad that displays plain-text diagnostics and status. Diagnostics are text messages, not numeric codes. Full list: IntelliPak Programming, Troubleshooting manual and IOM RT-SVX36. Coverage is partial: the IntelliPak I/II UCM diagnostic list (RT-SVP07 / RT-SVX36 / RT-SVX30, up to 56 diagnostic points) also includes items not transcribed here because no source text was seen: GBAS communication failure, exhaust/return-fan static and IGV/VFD faults, CO2 sensor failure, waterside items on self-contained units, supply-air-temperature high/low limits and heat-module gas-specific diagnostics. Several diagnostic descriptions were read from the IntelliPak Signature Series (self-contained) Installation, Owner and Diagnostic Manual (ManualsLib 534679 pp.97-102) and the SCWG modular-series diagnostic pages; these units use the same RTM/HI UCM firmware family and identical diagnostic text, but rooftop-only items (Compressor Trip, fan proving, Emergency Stop, LPC lockout, Frostat) were taken from rooftop documents. The 'SCM / MCM Communication Failure' description is quoted from the help-center MCM article written for the same 1U49 MCM on CGAF-family units; the rooftop diagnostic text itself was only seen as an index entry.

faultCodes.code: HI COMMUNICATIONS FAILURE - CHECK INTERPROCESSOR COMM LINK
faultCodes.meaning: The unit-mounted Human Interface (HI, 1U65) is not communicating with the RoofTop Module (RTM, 1U48 IntelliPak I / 1U1 IntelliPak II). Causes can include wiring errors such as shorted comm links, excessive noise on the comm link, a defective HI, defective modules other than the HI, or the RTM power supply shorted out. Electrical noise from VFDs or unit high-voltage wiring can cause communication problems; comm link wires should be separated from high-voltage power wiring as much as possible.
likelyCauses: Shorted, open or reversed interprocessor communication (IPC) link wiring
Noise coupled from VFD / power wiring routed with the comm link
A failed module (other than the HI) loading down the shared comm bus
RTM power supply shorted / RTM unpowered
Failed HI
checks: Check the IPC link at the HI and RTM (polarity, shield, terminations, separation from power wiring)
Verify RTM power and the RTM power LED; disconnect other modules one at a time from the comm link to find one that is loading the bus (manufacturer procedure)
Cycle power and watch whether the HI re-establishes communication
faultCodes.source: Trane Help Center - IntelliPak (Legacy) HI Comm Loss (19893668115853)

faultCodes.meaning: The RTM has lost communication with the heat module. An 'all heat off' request is sent to the heat operation function. If the unit has staged gas or electric heat, all heat module outputs are zeroed and de-energized. If the unit has hydronic heat or chilled water, the unit turns off the supply fan and closes the outside air damper upon the occurrence of a heat module comm failure.
likelyCauses: IPC comm link wiring to the heat module (1U50 IntelliPak I)
Heat module unpowered (fuse/transformer) or failed
Module DIP / address setting wrong after replacement
checks: Check 24 VAC power and the comm link at the heat module; check address settings
Automatic reset when communication is restored
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak SCWG diagnostic troubleshooting (manualsdir 213839 p.114); Trane IntelliPak I Programming manual (ManualsLib 865947) diagnostics

faultCodes.meaning: Displayed on the HI when the freezestat (4S12) closes its contacts because the temperature of the air entering the heating coils falls to 40 F (hydronic/steam heat units): it signals the Heat Module (1U50) to turn off the supply fan and initiate a 'Heat Fail' diagnostic displayed on the Human Interface LCD screen; a manual reset is initiated. On gas heat units, if the ignition system does not detect a flame during operation or loses flame it locks out the heating system; a flame failure is reset by pressing the reset button on the front of the IC (ignition control) board case.
likelyCauses: Hydronic/steam: loss of hot water or steam to the coil, control valve failed closed, coil airflow with heat off at low outdoor temperature
Gas: ignition control lockout (no flame / flame loss), high temperature limit open, gas supply or pressure switch problem
checks: Hydronic: check heating-medium supply and valve position; verify freezestat 4S12 setting/contacts and reset after the coil warms
Gas: check the IC board LED/reset button, flame sensor, gas pressure and high limits, then reset the IC board and the HI diagnostic
faultCodes.source: RT-SVX36 IOM (ManualsLib 687076) freezestat 4S12 / Heat Fail and gas flame failure reset

faultCodes.code: Compressor Trip Ckt #1 / Ckt #2 (also Ckt #3, #4 on 4-circuit units)
faultCodes.meaning: A Compressor Trip occurs if the compressor proving input(s) on the SCM/MCM (1U49 IntelliPak I / 1U3 IntelliPak II) does not close within three seconds of the call for a compressor to start, or the input opens for 3 seconds during compressor operation. The input is connected to the normally open contacts of an auxiliary switch on the side of the lead compressor contactor on each circuit. This is a manual reset diagnostic. On units with later RTM/MCM versions (typically built or ordered after 02/2009) the circuit is allowed to retry after 15 minutes and goes to a Compressor Trip diagnostic on the 4th occurrence.
likelyCauses: Any safety device in the contactor coil circuit open: high-pressure cutout (HPC), compressor winding temperature limit, Compressor Protection Module (CPM), or compressor circuit breaker - the contactor (or K42 on variable-speed-compressor units) cannot energize so the proving input never closes
Failed or misadjusted auxiliary switch on the lead compressor contactor, or wiring between the aux switch and the SCM/MCM
Low refrigerant charge causing the winding thermostat (motor overload) to open
On VSC / VFD units: failed K42 relay on the drive (help-center K42 article)
Failed SCM/MCM input
checks: At the HI read which circuit tripped; check the HPC, winding thermostat / CPM and compressor circuit breaker for that circuit before resetting (manufacturer procedure)

Verify wiring between the contactor auxiliary switch and the SCM/MCM proving input; with the contactor energized (Service Mode can force the circuit on) confirm the aux contacts close and the HI shows the input closed
If safeties are closed and the aux switch proves, check 24 VAC to the contactor coil and the contactor itself
Field practice: if the HPC tripped, check condenser fans/coil and charge before clearing; if the winding stat tripped, check charge, superheat and compressor amps
Reset at the HI (DIAGNOSTICS / reset active manual diagnostics, password protected) or by cycling power to the RTM
faultCodes.source: Trane Help Center - Legacy IntelliPak Compressor Trip Diagnostics (16077839043085); RT-SVX36 IOM (ManualsLib 687076) safety devices; Help Center K42 relay article (16077950185101)

faultCodes.meaning: This diagnostic occurs if the compressor proving input(s) on the SCM/MCM (1U49) does not open within three seconds of the call for the lead compressor on a circuit to stop, or the input is closed when all compressors on a circuit should be off. The unit controls assume that the compressor contactor has welded closed.
likelyCauses: Welded / stuck compressor contactor
Auxiliary switch on the contactor stuck closed or miswired
SCM/MCM proving input failed
checks: With the circuit commanded off, confirm the contactor has dropped out and the compressor is not running; if it is, replace the contactor
Check the auxiliary switch contacts open with the contactor de-energized
Manufacturer test: if jumpering / opening the input makes the diagnostic appear and clear, the input/board is good; if not, replace the SCM/MCM (1U49)
faultCodes.source: Trane Help Center - Compressor Contactor Failure (34759305864205), SCM/MCM 1U49 proving input

faultCodes.code: Low Pressure Cutout Ckt #1 / Ckt #2 (LPC lockout)
faultCodes.meaning: The Ckt # LPC input is detected open as described in the compressor protection function; a 'Lockout Ckt #1, 2, 3 or 4' request is issued to the compressor staging control function. Protection function: when the LPC is opened for 1 continuous second the compressor for that circuit is turned off immediately and is not allowed to restart for a minimum of 3 minutes; if four consecutive open conditions occur during an active call for cooling the compressor is locked out, a diagnostic generated, and a manual reset required. The diagnostic can be reset by the Human Interface or Tracer Summit.
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge / leak
Restricted liquid line, TXV or filter drier; low evaporator airflow (dirty filters, coil, fan problem)
Low ambient operation without head-pressure control
Failed LPC switch or open wiring to the SCM/MCM
checks: Check the 'Disabled by Low Pressure Cutout' status and LPC input state at the HI
Gauge the circuit: suction pressure at start-up and running, superheat/subcooling; look for a leak if charge is low (field practice)
Verify airflow: filters, evaporator coil, supply fan proving and VFD/IGV position
Check the LPC switch continuity and wiring; reset at the HI after correcting the cause
faultCodes.source: RT-SVX36 IOM (ManualsLib 687076) compressor protection / Low Pressure Control; IntelliPak SCWG diagnostic troubleshooting (manualsdir 213839 p.114); IntelliPak I Programming manual (ManualsLib 865947 p.31 Disable Or Lockout Sources)

faultCodes.meaning: The supply airflow input is detected OPEN for 40 continuous seconds during any period of time in which the supply fan binary output is ON (the differential switch of the supply airflow proving switch 3S68 detected open for 40 consecutive seconds during a request for fan operation). A manual reset diagnostic is initiated and the RTM shuts off all system functions.
likelyCauses: Supply fan not running: VFD fault, K42 relay on the VFD failed (help-center article), fan contactor, belts, motor overload
Airflow proving switch 3S68 misadjusted, plugged tubing, or wiring open
Inlet guide vanes closed / VFD at minimum so the differential is below the switch setpoint
checks: Confirm the fan actually runs on a fan request (Service Mode); check VFD display/fault, K42, belts and overloads
Check the 3S68 differential switch tubing and setpoint; verify the input closes at the RTM when the fan is running
Reset at the HI or by cycling RTM power after correcting the cause
faultCodes.source: RT-SVX36 IOM (ManualsLib 687076) supply airflow proving 3S68 / manual reset diagnostics; Help Center K42 relay article (16077950185101)

faultCodes.meaning: The exhaust fan airflow proving switch (3S69) is a binary input used on units with an exhaust fan and signals the RTM when the exhaust fan is operating. If an open fan proving switch is detected the RTM shuts off all system functions; for an exhaust fan failure (3S69) a manual reset diagnostic is initiated.
likelyCauses: Exhaust fan not running (contactor, VFD/K42, belts, overload)
3S69 proving switch misadjusted, tubing or wiring open
Exhaust dampers not opening so the switch never proves
checks: Force the exhaust fan on in Service Mode and verify rotation, belts and damper travel
Check the 3S69 switch setpoint/tubing and confirm the RTM input closes with the fan running
Reset at the HI after correction
faultCodes.source: RT-SVX36 IOM (ManualsLib 687076) exhaust fan airflow proving 3S69 / manual reset diagnostics

faultCodes.meaning: An open circuit has occurred on the emergency stop input caused either by a high duct temp t-stat trip, or the opening of field-provided contacts/switch, etc.; the unit stops immediately. Emergency Stop is manual reset (requires reset at the Human Interface). High Duct Temp Thermostats (3S16, 3S17) provide a high limit shutdown if the supply air temperature reaches 240 F or the return air temperature reaches 135 F.
likelyCauses: High duct temperature thermostat 3S16 (supply, 240 F) or 3S17 (return, 135 F) tripped - fire or overheating condition
Field fire-alarm / smoke contacts opened
Broken or removed field jumper / wiring on the emergency stop terminals
checks: Check the emergency stop input terminals for continuity; identify which device opened (duct stats vs field contacts)
If a duct stat tripped, inspect for a real overheating event (gas heat overfiring, low airflow) before resetting
Reset at the HI DIAGNOSTICS menu (manual reset)
faultCodes.source: Trane IntelliPak SCWF 20 IOM (ManualsLib 1422639 p.103) Emergency Stop diagnostic; Help Center Equipment/External Auto Stop vs Emergency Stop (27517129655309); RT-SVX36 IOM (ManualsLib 687076) high duct temp thermostats

faultCodes.code: External Auto Stop / Equipment Stop (input open)
faultCodes.meaning: External Stop and Emergency Stop inputs both cause the unit to stop immediately; External (Equipment) Auto Stop is Auto Reset - the diagnostic automatically resets when the External Auto/Stop input is re-closed and the unit returns to the current operating mode.
likelyCauses: Fire alarm management system, time clock or BAS contact open on the external stop input
Missing factory jumper on unused external stop terminals
checks: Verify the field contact / jumper on the external stop terminals; the diagnostic clears itself when the input closes
faultCodes.source: Trane Help Center - Equipment / External Auto Stop versus Emergency Stop (IntelliPak 20-162) (27517129655309)

faultCodes.meaning: If the RTM sees a closed dirty-filter pressure switch for 60 seconds it sets the alarm; if it sees the switch open for 60 seconds the alarm is cleared. It does not shut down the unit; it is a warning that the filters may need service (displayed as an alarm on the HI and can drive an alarm output).
likelyCauses: Loaded filters
Filter switch set too low, tubing reversed or plugged
High-static VAV operation at full fan speed
checks: Change filters; verify the switch resets after 60 s with the fan running
Check switch setpoint against the filter bank pressure drop with clean filters
faultCodes.source: Trane Help Center IntelliPak (Legacy) section - Intellipak Dirty Filter Alarm Diagnostic

faultCodes.meaning: The RTM has lost communication with the compressor module (SCM single-circuit / MCM multi-circuit, 1U49 IntelliPak I / 1U3 IntelliPak II). The help-center description for the same module on IntelliPak-controlled units: the MCM (1U49) is not communicating with the master module; causes are (a) wiring error, (b) defective MCM, or (c) no control power to the MCM. All modules share a comm link using twisted wire; the J1 connector on each module is the connection point, all landing on a common terminal strip.
likelyCauses: Comm link (J1) wiring open/shorted at the SCM/MCM
No 24 VAC control power to the SCM/MCM
Defective SCM/MCM
checks: Check control power at the SCM/MCM and the J1 comm connector; check the common comm terminal strip
If power and wiring are good and the module still does not communicate, replace the SCM/MCM
Compressors will not run without the compressor module communicating; auto reset when comm returns
faultCodes.source: Trane IntelliPak I Programming manual (ManualsLib 865947) index - SCM and MCM Communication Failure; Trane Help Center - MCM Communications Failure (34791196533645) (description written for the CGAF/IntelliPak MCM 1U49)

faultCodes.meaning: The RTM has lost communications with the ECEM (Exhaust/Comparative Enthalpy Module). If the unit has the Comparative Enthalpy option, an automatic reset occurs after communication has been restored.
likelyCauses: Comm link wiring / power to the ECEM
Failed ECEM
checks: Check power and comm link at the ECEM; economizer falls back to dry-bulb changeover meanwhile
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak SCWG diagnostic troubleshooting (manualsdir 213839); IntelliPak Signature Series diagnostic manual (ManualsLib 534679 pp.97-102)

faultCodes.meaning: The RTM has lost communications with the VOM (Ventilation Override Module, 1U53 IntelliPak I / 1U8 IntelliPak II). Ventilation override actions will not be allowed, and the VO Output relay will be de-energized. An automatic reset occurs after communication has been restored.
likelyCauses: Comm link wiring / power to the VOM
Failed VOM
checks: Check power and comm link at the VOM; auto reset when comm returns
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak Signature Series diagnostic manual (ManualsLib 534679 p.102) VOM Communications Failure; IntelliPak SCWG diagnostic troubleshooting (manualsdir 213839 p.118)

faultCodes.meaning: The RTM has lost communication with the VCM (Ventilation Control Module). All active commands and setpoints provided by the VCM are canceled and/or ignored; a fail-safe function in the VCM causes all of its outputs to de-energize and/or be set to zero.
likelyCauses: Comm link wiring / power to the VCM
Failed VCM
checks: Check power and comm link at the VCM; Traq / DCV / preheat functions are lost until comm is restored (auto reset)
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak Signature Series diagnostic manual (ManualsLib 534679 p.102) VCM Communication Failure; IntelliPak SCWG diagnostic troubleshooting (manualsdir 213839 p.118)

faultCodes.meaning: The RTM has lost communications with the Night Setback Panel (programmable zone sensor).
likelyCauses: Programmable zone sensor (NSB panel) comm wiring open/shorted
NSB panel unpowered or failed
checks: Check the NSB panel comm wiring and power; auto reset when comm returns
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak Signature Series diagnostic manual (ManualsLib 534679 p.99) NSB Panel Comm Failure

faultCodes.meaning: An error occurred while the RTM was writing data to its internal non-volatile memory (EEPROM). An information-only diagnostic is displayed at the Human Interface. A manual reset may be made at the Human Interface, at Tracer Summit, or by cycling power to the RTM.
likelyCauses: Power interruption during a setpoint/configuration write
Failing RTM EEPROM / RTM
checks: Reset; verify setpoints and configuration were retained. If it recurs, replace the RTM (field practice)
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak Signature Series diagnostic manual (ManualsLib 534679 p.100) RTM Data Storage Error

faultCodes.meaning: The RTM Auxiliary Temperature Sensor data is out of range. Sensor resistance should be between 830 ohms (200 F) and 345.7 kohms (-40 F) (Trane 10 kohm at 77 F thermistor).
likelyCauses: Open or shorted sensor / wiring
Sensor not installed but the function that uses it is enabled
checks: Ohm the sensor at the RTM terminals and compare to the thermistor curve; check wiring; auto reset when in range
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak Signature Series diagnostic manual (ManualsLib 534679 p.100) RTM Aux. Temp. Sensor Failure; thermistor range from SCWF IOM (ManualsLib 1422639 p.104)

faultCodes.code: RTM Zone Sensor Failure (RTM Zone Temp Sensor Failure)
faultCodes.meaning: The RTM zone temperature sensor input is out of range (diagnostic listed on the same page as RTM Aux. Temp. Sensor Failure, whose text reads 'data is out of range'; the zone sensor is the standard Trane 10 kohm at 77 F thermistor and the diagnostic clears when the RTM again reads a valid sensor). 'RTM Zone Temp Sensor Failure' is one of the diagnostics assignable to the RTM/MCM alarm outputs.
likelyCauses: Open/shorted zone sensor wiring, sensor removed or wrong sensor type
Zone sensor source selected at the HI does not match the installed sensor
checks: Ohm the zone sensor at the RTM (about 10 kohm at 77 F); check wiring; verify the zone temperature source setting
Unit falls back per setup (supply-air control units continue; zone-control units lose zone temp) - auto reset when the input returns to range
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak Signature Series diagnostic manual (ManualsLib 534679 p.100) RTM Zone Sensor Failure; IntelliPak I Programming manual (ManualsLib 865947 p.75) MCM alarm assignment values

faultCodes.meaning: Supply air temperature sensor input failed / out of range. Listed as a diagnostic assignable to the RTM and MCM alarm outputs ('Supply Air Temp Sensor Failure') in the IntelliPak I programming manual.
likelyCauses: Open/shorted supply air sensor or wiring (sensor in the supply fan discharge)
Sensor unplugged at the RTM
checks: Ohm the sensor (10 kohm at 77 F thermistor) and check wiring to the RTM; view the SA temp on the HI Status menu
Supply-air-temperature control (VAV units) cannot operate correctly without it; auto reset when in range
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak I Programming manual (ManualsLib 865947 p.75) Assignment Submenu - MCM Alarms possible values

faultCodes.meaning: The return air temperature sensor reading is outside the acceptable range (diagnostic listed on p.99 of the Signature Series diagnostic manual).
likelyCauses: Open/shorted return air sensor or wiring
Sensor not installed (option-dependent)
checks: Ohm the sensor and wiring; auto reset when in range
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak Signature Series diagnostic manual (ManualsLib 534679 p.99) Return Air Temp Sensor Failure

faultCodes.meaning: There is not a valid signal on the outdoor air temperature input (outdoor air temperature sensor data out of range).
likelyCauses: Open/shorted OA sensor or wiring; sensor damaged by weather
Wrong sensor type
checks: Check the OA temperature reading at the HI; ohm the sensor and wiring; substitute a resistor at the module to prove the input
Economizer and low-ambient functions that depend on OA temp are affected; auto reset when in range
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak Signature Series diagnostic manual (ManualsLib 534679 p.99) O/A Temp. Sensor Failure; Trane Help Center CGM OA Temperature Sensor Failure (23499896877453) description of the same input

faultCodes.meaning: The outdoor air humidity sensor input is out of range. If this sensor fails it will not lock out the unit; it is only used for economizer (comparative/reference enthalpy) control.
likelyCauses: Failed OA humidity sensor (located behind the outdoor air intakes) or its wiring
Sensor not installed but comparative enthalpy configured
checks: Check the sensor output and wiring; economizer runs on dry-bulb changeover until repaired
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak Signature Series diagnostic manual (ManualsLib 534679 p.99) O/A Humidity Sensor Failure; HVAC-Talk 'Help with Intellipak' (99790) field description

faultCodes.meaning: The active space static pressure setpoint is out of range - the unit is reading a signal that is out of range for the space static pressure setpoint (input < 0.03 IWC or input > 0.20 IWC). If the space pressure setpoint source is GBAS but this setpoint has not been assigned to any of the 4 analog inputs on the GBAS, this message will occur. The default space pressure setpoint becomes the active space pressure setpoint; an automatic reset occurs after the designated setpoint source sends a signal within range for 10 continuous seconds, or after a different setpoint source is user-defined.
likelyCauses: GBAS analog input not assigned / BAS sending an out-of-range value
Setpoint entered outside 0.03-0.20 IWC
checks: Check the setpoint value and its source at the HI SETPOINTS/SETUP menus; assign the GBAS input or change the source
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak Signature Series diagnostic manual (ManualsLib 534679 p.100) Space Static Press Setpt Failure

faultCodes.meaning: The space static pressure sensor is used on units with 100% exhaust with Statitrac. The diagnostic occurs when the voltage output from the transducer is outside the range for normal building pressures (-0.67 IWC to 0.67 IWC): during normal operation if the voltage dips below 0.04 VDC or rises above 0.75 VDC the diagnostic is generated. It can also be generated if the calibration solenoid is not functioning properly.
likelyCauses: Space pressure tubing plugged, kinked, disconnected or reference tube open to wind
Calibration solenoid failed
Transducer failed or wiring open
checks: Measure the transducer output at the module; confirm it moves with pressure and returns to the zero value when the calibration solenoid energizes
Check tubing to the space and the outdoor reference; do not confuse the space and supply-duct transducers (mounted side by side)
faultCodes.source: Trane Help Center - Intellipak w/ Symbio 800 - Space Pressure Reading Faults (19743333794317) transducer description (same Statitrac transducer); IntelliPak (Legacy) section lists 'Space Pressure Sensor Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Diagnostic listed in the IntelliPak (Legacy) help-center section: the supply duct static pressure transducer signal is not valid. Manufacturer transducer test: if the voltage does not change when the pressure changes, the transducer is bad; a valid zero-pressure reading is 0.25 +/- 0.06 VDC and the valid operating range is 0.25 to 1.75 VDC.
likelyCauses: Supply duct pressure tubing disconnected/plugged (usually an air leak, mispiping or plugged tube)
Transducer failed or wiring open
Tubing landed on the wrong transducer (supply and space transducers are side by side)
checks: Read the transducer output at the RTM; verify ~0.25 VDC with tubes disconnected and a rising voltage with duct pressure (manometer in parallel)
Check tubing routing to the duct tap; VAV units cannot control fan speed / IGV without it
faultCodes.source: Trane Help Center IntelliPak (Legacy) section - Supply Air Pressure Sensor Failure; Help Center Flow sensor failure / pressure transducer troubleshooting (16077694845069)

faultCodes.code: Velocity Sensor Failure (Traq / VCM velocity pressure)
faultCodes.meaning: The velocity pressure input signal is out of range - the unit is reading a signal that is out of range for the velocity pressure transducer input on the VCM. Check field/unit wiring between the sensor and the VCM.
likelyCauses: Air leak, mispiping or plugged tube between the Traq flow ring and the transducer (most common)
Calibration solenoid bad
Transducer or VCM defective (rare)
checks: Manufacturer test: connect a manometer in parallel to the transducer (high to high, low to low); expect 0.05-1.75 IWC depending on OA flow and 0 IWC when the calibration solenoid is energized; zero-flow voltage 0.25 +/- 0.06 VDC, operating range 0.25-1.75 VDC
If the voltage does not track pressure, replace the transducer
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak SCWG diagnostic troubleshooting (manualsdir 213839 p.118) Velocity Sensor Failure; Trane Help Center IntelliPak (Legacy) Traq flow sensor / Velocity Sensor Failures (16077962622477)

faultCodes.code: Evap Temp Sensor Failure Ckt # (coil frost sensor)
faultCodes.meaning: The evaporator temperature sensor (ckt #1, 2, 3 or 4) is out of range. Sensor resistance should be between 830 ohms (200 F) and 345.7 kohms (-40 F). The coil frost protection function for that refrigeration circuit only is disabled. An automatic reset occurs after the evaporator temp input returns to its allowable range for 10 seconds.
likelyCauses: Open/shorted coil thermistor or wiring to the SCM/MCM
Sensor pulled out of the coil well
checks: Ohm the sensor at the compressor module; check wiring; the circuit keeps running but without Frostat coil-frost protection until repaired
faultCodes.source: Trane IntelliPak SCWF 20 IOM (ManualsLib 1422639 p.104) evaporator temperature sensor diagnostic; RT-SVX36 IOM (ManualsLib 687076) Frostat coil frost protection

faultCodes.code: Disabled By Ckt # Evap Low Limit (coil frost cutout)
faultCodes.meaning: Status shown under Disable Or Lockout Sources: 'Disabled By Ckt - Evap Low Limit: entering evaporator temp is excessively low' (Coil Frost Cutout Temperature setpoint, default 30 F, shuts off the circuit's compressors to prevent freezing); 'Disabled By Evap Temp Sensor Fail' is shown when the sensor itself has failed.
likelyCauses: Low airflow across the evaporator (filters, fan speed, closed VAV boxes)
Low refrigerant charge
Low supply air setpoint at low load
checks: Check airflow and charge; review the coil frost cutout setpoint at the HI; the circuit re-enables automatically when the coil warms
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak I Programming manual (ManualsLib 865947 p.31 Disable Or Lockout Sources; p.57 Coil Frost Cutout Temperature)

faultCodes.code: Supply Air Static Pressure Limit - auto reset (SA Static Press Limit)
faultCodes.meaning: VAV units: the supply air static pressure exceeded the supply air pressure high limit setpoint (field example 4.0 IWC); the unit shuts down and this auto-reset diagnostic restarts it. 'Auto Reset SA Static Pres Limit' is an assignable alarm value.
likelyCauses: VAV boxes closed (coming out of night setback / morning warm-up) with the fan at full speed
Static setpoint or high limit set too low / too close; IGV or VFD control loop mis-tuned
Plugged or disconnected duct pressure tubing giving a false high reading
Fire/smoke damper closed
checks: Compare the HI duct static reading with a manometer at the duct tap; check tubing
Verify VAV boxes open on a fan start and the VFD/IGV minimum settings; review the high limit and static setpoints
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak I Programming manual (ManualsLib 865947 p.119) supply air static pressure limit diagnostic; RTM alarm assignment values (p.74); HVAC-Talk 'Trane Intellipak Question' (545632) field example of the 4.0 IWC high limit

faultCodes.code: Supply Air Static Pressure Limit - manual reset
faultCodes.meaning: The auto reset supply air static pressure limit diagnostic has occurred for the third time while the unit is operating in occupied mode; a 'supply air pressure shutdown' signal is sent to the unit functions and a manual reset is required anytime after the diagnostic is set.
likelyCauses: Same causes as the auto-reset limit, recurring three times in occupied mode
checks: Correct the cause of the repeated high-static trips, then reset at the HI (password protected) or by cycling RTM power
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak I Programming manual (ManualsLib 865947 p.119) supply air static pressure limit diagnostic

faultCodes.meaning: The cooling setpoint input is out of range (Occupied Zone Cool SETPOINT Failure).
likelyCauses: Zone sensor cooling setpoint slider/thumbwheel open or shorted
Setpoint source set to a sensor/GBAS input that is not installed
checks: Check the setpoint source at the HI SETUP menu; ohm the zone sensor setpoint potentiometer; the unit uses the default/HI setpoint until the input returns to range (auto reset)
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak I Programming manual (ManualsLib 865947) diagnostics - Unoccupied/Occupied Zone Cool Setpoint Failure

faultCodes.meaning: The heating setpoint input is out of range for the Active Occupied Zone Heating setpoint.
likelyCauses: Zone sensor heating setpoint slider/thumbwheel open or shorted
Setpoint source not installed / not assigned
checks: Check the setpoint source at the HI; ohm the zone sensor setpoint potentiometer; auto reset when in range
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak I Programming manual (ManualsLib 865947) diagnostics - zone heating setpoint failure

faultCodes.meaning: The Unoccupied Zone Cooling Setpoint Input Is Out Of Range.
likelyCauses: Unoccupied setpoint source (NSB panel / GBAS) not installed or not assigned
Out-of-range value from the BAS
checks: Check the unoccupied setpoint source at the HI; a constant automatic-reset 'Unocc Cool Setpoint Fail' usually means the source is set to a sensor or BAS input that is not present (field reports)
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak Signature Series diagnostic manual (ManualsLib 534679 p.102) Unoccupied Zone Cool Setpoint Failure; HVAC-Talk field report (481332)

faultCodes.meaning: The heating setpoint input is out of range for the Active Unoccupied Zone Heating setpoint.
likelyCauses: Unoccupied setpoint source (NSB panel / GBAS) not installed or not assigned
checks: Check the unoccupied heating setpoint source at the HI; auto reset when in range
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak Signature Series diagnostic manual (ManualsLib 534679 p.102) Unoccupied Zone Heat Setpoint Failure; IntelliPak I Programming manual (ManualsLib 865947)

faultCodes.code: Supply Air Temp Cool Setpoint Failure
faultCodes.meaning: The supply air temperature cooling setpoint input is out of range (listed as 'Supply Air Temp Cool Setpoint Fail' in the diagnostic troubleshooting list).
likelyCauses: Setpoint source (GBAS analog input / BAS) not assigned or out of range
checks: Check the SA cooling setpoint source and value at the HI; the default setpoint is used until the input is valid
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak Signature Series diagnostic manual (ManualsLib 534679 p.101) Supply Air Temp Cool Setpoint Fail

diagnosticTips: Diagnostics and mode status are read on the unit-mounted Human Interface LCD (Diagnostics menu) or a remote HI panel; alarm relays can be configured for BAS.
Common IPC (interprocessor communication) faults are usually wiring/termination problems at the modules; check the link before replacing modules.
Full diagnostic text list and troubleshooting trees: IntelliPak I Programming, Troubleshooting manual and IOM RT-SVX36M-EN (Trane eLibrary).

IntelliPak diagnostics are plain-text messages on the unit-mounted Human Interface (HI, 1U65: 2 line x 40 character LCD with a 16-key keypad) or a Remote HI panel; there are no numeric codes. Main menu keys: STATUS, SETPOINTS, SETUP, CONFIGURATION, DIAGNOSTICS, SERVICE MODE (plus CUSTOM). Press DIAGNOSTICS to see the active diagnostics list and step through them with the NEXT/PREVIOUS keys; the Status menu shows 'Disable or Lockout Sources' for each function (e.g. Disabled By Low Pressure Cutout, Disabled By Ckt - Evap Low Limit).

Reset: manual-reset (PMR) diagnostics are cleared from the HI DIAGNOSTICS menu or by cycling power to the RTM. On the 'Diagnostic Reset Is Password Protected' screen enter the password with the + / - keys and press ENTER; the HI shows 'Resetting Active Manual Diagnostics Sending Reset Request' then 'Updating Unit Data, Please wait'. Diagnostics can also be reset from Tracer Summit. Automatic-reset diagnostics clear themselves when the input returns to range (typically for 10-15 continuous seconds).

SERVICE MODE (local HI only, not available on the Remote HI) lets you force the supply fan, exhaust, economizer, individual compressor circuits and heat stages to test them and to reproduce a lockout (e.g. turn on the circuit that tripped while watching the proving input).

Module designators: IntelliPak I - RTM 1U48, SCM/MCM 1U49, Heat 1U50, VOM 1U53, HI 1U65; IntelliPak II - RTM 1U1, SCM/MCM 1U3, VOM 1U8. All modules share one twisted-pair interprocessor comm link landed on a common terminal strip; most 'Communication Failure' diagnostics are wiring, module power or VFD noise problems - keep the comm link away from power wiring.

Gas heat: flame failure locks out at the ignition control (IC) board and is reset with the button on the front of the IC board case, then reset the HI diagnostic. High duct temperature thermostats 3S16 (240 F supply) / 3S17 (135 F return) open the Emergency Stop input.

ledPatterns.pattern: IntelliPak module power LED off (RTM/SCM/MCM/Heat/VCM/VOM)
ledPatterns.meaning: Module unpowered - check the 24 VAC fuse/transformer feeding that module; the HI will show a communication failure for it
checks: Check module power and the shared J1 comm link before replacing the module

controls.name: Trane Symbio 800 unit controller (IntelliPak)
controls.description: Touchscreen (TD7) unit controller on IntelliPak 1 / IntelliPak 3 rooftops and RAUK from the late 2010s (RT-SVP011 'IntelliPak with Symbio 800'). Diagnostics are plain-text alarms on the TD7 touchscreen (Active Alarms / Historic Alarms) and in Tracer TU, similar in style to Symbio 700. Entries below are the diagnostics whose meaning was visible in a Trane help-center article or the RT-SVP011 troubleshooting table; the full table (Diagnostic, Target, Severity, Persistence, Condition/Response, Reset Level) in RT-SVP011G-EN was not transcribed, so coverage is partial. Confidence stays low until the RT-SVP011 table is read. Controller hardware status (added from the Symbio 800 IOM BAS-SVX080E-EN, high confidence): the Status/P1-P3/IMC/Ethernet LEDs, the 7-segment boot/status codes and the firmware-update 'F' failure codes apply to every Symbio 800 application (IntelliPak, RTHD/RTWD/RTZA/Ascend chillers, SCWM self-contained). Unit-specific Symbio 800 diagnostics for chillers and SCWM are in their own platforms (trane_rthd_symbio800, trane_rtza_symbio800, trane_ascend_symbio800, trane_scwm_symbio800).

faultCodes.code: Supply Fan X Proving Failure / Relief Fan Proving Failure (Symbio 800, IntelliPak)
faultCodes.meaning: IntelliPak with Symbio 800 diagnostic raised when the supply (or relief/exhaust) fan is commanded but airflow is not proven. Trane help center: the Combustion Fan Proving Switch and the Supply Air Proving Switch (3S14) are wired in series; 3S14 is often the culprit at the beginning of the ignition sequence as it is a differential pressure switch that should close at 0.20 iwc (closed with the supply fan at 22 Hz or greater).
likelyCauses: Supply fan VFD never started (VFD fault, run command/Modbus problem) — check the VFD diagnostic log, parameter 15-30
Supply air proving switch 3S14 out of adjustment, tubing loose on the high port, or the red cap not removed from the low port
Low duct static in SZVAV applications or with a panel removed during heat-exchanger oil burn-off
Broken belt, motor overload, blown fuses
checks: Confirm the VFD is running and check its diagnostic log (parameter 15-30) for a VFD-side fault
Test the proving switch with a squeeze bulb or by ramping the fan; it should be open with the fan off and closed at 22 Hz or above; adjust sensitivity if needed
Verify the tubing on the high port and that the low-port red cap was removed
On SZVAV with firmware >= 1.30.008 increase the Heating Min Discharge Air Flow Setpoint in service settings until the switch closes
faultCodes.source: Trane help center 'Intellipak with Symbio 800 controls Supply and Relief Fan Proving Failure' (article 16077871063053); 'Intellipak Symbio Combustion Fan proving switch' (article 31150918286733); IntelliPak with Symbio 800 Programming Guide RT-SVP011 troubleshooting table
faultCodes.notes: Symbio 800 alarms display on the TD7 front panel under Active Alarms / Historic Alarms; full table in RT-SVP011 (Diagnostic, Target, Severity, Persistence, Condition/Response, Reset Level).

faultCodes.meaning: IntelliPak with Symbio 800 diagnostic triggered when a fixed-speed compressor fails to prove off for 6 continuous seconds (proving input still indicates running after the compressor is commanded off).
likelyCauses: Welded compressor contactor
Proving input (current sensor / aux contact) stuck or miswired
checks: With the compressor commanded off, check whether the contactor is still pulled in and the compressor still draws current
Verify the proving device and its wiring to the compressor module; replace the contactor if welded
faultCodes.source: IntelliPak with Symbio 800 Programming Guide (RT-SVP011; ManualsLib 2901605 p.86 troubleshooting diagnostics)

faultCodes.code: Loss of Charge Warning / Loss of Charge Lockout (Symbio 800, IntelliPak / RAUK)
faultCodes.meaning: Symbio 800 refrigeration diagnostics for a circuit that appears to have lost charge. Per Trane, firmware 4.10.002 (Oct 2024) enhanced the loss-of-charge algorithm: the Loss of Charge Warning no longer triggers in active Reheat or Hot Gas Bypass, Loss of Charge Detection became a non-latching warning with detection time extended from 300 to 1800 seconds, and the Loss of Charge Lockout diagnostic time was extended from 300 to 900 seconds. During a lockout the circuit is inhibited from starting and running but may be allowed to start if the diagnostic condition is cleared.
likelyCauses: Actual refrigerant leak / low charge
Nuisance trips on older firmware (< 4.10.002), especially during reheat or hot gas bypass operation
Suction/discharge pressure transducer error or wiring
checks: Verify charge with gauges (subcooling/superheat) before resetting; leak-check if low
Compare the transducer readings on the display to gauge readings; check transducer wiring
Update Symbio 800 firmware to 4.10.002 or later if nuisance alarms occur in reheat/HGBP
faultCodes.source: Trane help center 'IntelliPak and RAUK with Symbio 800 – Loss of Charge Diagnostics and Other Refrigeration issues' (article 31263569395981)

faultCodes.code: Airflow Press X Measurement Failure (Traq flow sensor, Symbio 800)
faultCodes.meaning: The 'Airflow Press X Measurement Failure' diagnostic (X = 1 or 2) indicates that the calibration solenoid is not responding correctly. The calibration solenoid is energized for one second every minute to zero out the transducer; if it is not functioning the controls do not receive the correct error signal and interpret the sensor reading as zero pressure.
likelyCauses: Calibration solenoid failed (most common)
Rarely: transducer failed or the SPACE PRESSURE/TRAQ LLID defective
Tubing leaks or disconnected
checks: Unplug both tubes from the transducer and read the voltage at the black and green wires at the transducer, or SIGNAL and GND at the SPACE PRESSURE/TRAQ LLID (J3-2, 3)
Verify the solenoid clicks once per minute; replace it if not
Replace the transducer or LLID only after the solenoid and tubing check good
faultCodes.source: Trane help center 'IntelliPak (Symbio 800) - How to troubleshoot a Traq Flow Sensor Failures' (article 25825742264461)

faultCodes.code: E09 (VB1285) / flash code 53 (VB1287) — gas heat controller pressure switch (Symbio 800, IntelliPak)
faultCodes.meaning: The supply air proving pressure switch closes at 0.20 iwc; if the duct static pressure is low the unit generates an E09 alarm on the VB1285 (modulating burner controller) or a '53' flash code on the VB1287 (staged burner controller). Commonly seen at unit start-up, when a panel has been removed to burn processing oil off the heat exchanger, or in SZVAV applications where operating duct static is low.
likelyCauses: Duct static below 0.20 iwc at the proving switch (SZVAV low airflow, open panel, low fan speed)
Proving switch tubing/cap problem or switch out of adjustment
checks: Verify with a squeeze bulb or ramp the supply fan up to test the proving switch (closes at 0.20 iwc)
SZVAV with Symbio 800 firmware 1.30.008 or higher: increase the Heating Min Discharge Air Flow Setpoint in service settings until the proving switch closes
Replace panels removed for oil burn-off before running heat
faultCodes.source: Trane help center 'IntelliPak Symbio 800 - E09 or 53 Alarm on Gas Heat Controller' (article 16077821301133)

faultCodes.code: Outdoor Air Flow / Duct Static Pressure alarms in Event Log with fan off (Symbio 800)
faultCodes.meaning: There are times when the supply fan is OFF and the Event Log shows Outdoor Air Flow and Duct Static alarms because the transducers monitoring these pressures sometimes read below the unit's configured minimum operating range of 0 CCFM or 0 iwc.
likelyCauses: Transducer zero drift / slightly negative reading with the fan off (nuisance)
Wiring, plug or supply-voltage problems at the transducer; tubing leaks or rainwater in the tubing from an improperly installed outside-air static reference
checks: Verify the wiring, plugs and voltages at the transducer
Verify factory tubing with no leaks and that the outside-air static reference is properly installed; if rainwater entered the tubing, correct the installation and dry it out
Ignore isolated fan-off events if the readings are correct with the fan running
faultCodes.source: Trane help center 'Symbio 800 - Outdoor Air Flow and Duct Static Pressure Alarms in Event Log' (article 34375539024781)

faultCodes.meaning: Emergency stop input active — unit shut down while the emergency-stop input is in the stop state (same behaviour as documented for Symbio 700; confirm text in RT-SVP011).
checks: Check the emergency-stop input status on the touchscreen and the field contact / smoke detector relay wiring
faultCodes.source: Trane IntelliPak with Symbio 800 RT-SVP011G-EN (not transcribed); behaviour per Symbio 700 help-center article 18777598342029
faultCodes.notes: LOW confidence: alarm text inferred from the Symbio 700 article; verify in RT-SVP011.

diagnosticTips: Symbio 800 (IntelliPak 1/3, RAUK): alarms are read on the TD7 touch display under Active Alarms / Historic Alarms; the programming guide RT-SVP011 troubleshooting table gives Diagnostic text, Target, Severity, Persistence, Condition/Response and Reset Level for every diagnostic, with hyperlinks to troubleshooting.
Alarms and reset are on the touchscreen (Alarms > Reset) or via Tracer TU service tool; full table in RT-SVP011G-EN (IntelliPak with Symbio 800).

Symbio 800 hardware: green Status LED = power; flashing red with three dancing bars = an active alarm exists; flashing red with 'F' + code = fatal error (service required); with 'H' + code = hardware failure (controller will probably need replacing). Dancing dashes = normal operation (BAS-SVX080E-EN).

Symbio 800 rotary switches 999 = forced return to factory defaults ('ForCE.' then 'CLEAr.'). 'HoLd.' = the main program crashed too many times in 24 h; contact tech support. 'rEC.' = booted in recovery mode.

Symbio 800 firmware update from USB: exactly one .scfx file is required (F12 = none found, F13 = more than one); F39 = the update file is for another device (e.g. an SC+ file on a Symbio 800); F31 = update not allowed by software maintenance plan expiration.

controls.name: Trane / American Standard residential communicating system alerts (System Alert Guide: Err/ERR, CFG, SOP, XLB, SCH, TSO; ComfortLink II, AccuLink, Link)
controls.description: Alerts shown by the communicating thermostats XL824, XL850, XL1050 and Link UX360 (and the American Standard AccuLink equivalents) for ComfortLink II / AccuLink / Link systems: indoor units (furnaces, air handlers, hydronic coils), outdoor units (incl. variable-speed IVSC drives), zoning, sensors and the thermostat itself. The thermostat shows 'Err 126.00'; the guide writes ERR.126.00. Severity in the guide: Critical = the system cannot operate as intended in one or more modes, service required (mapped here to 'shutdown'); Major = performance or behaviour affected (mapped to 'warning'); Normal = informational, expected occasionally (mapped to 'info'). All 303 distinct alerts of the 08/05/2020 guide are included (the guide's table extraction had one duplicate SOP.004.00 row, dropped). The older ComfortLink II CL2.xxx.xx numbering is platform trane_res_comfortlink_ii_cl2 (most numbers are the same). Meaning = alarm description + problem description; checks = the guide's possible cause / corrective action column, as printed.
appliesTo: Trane XL824 (TCONT824), XL850, XL1050 (TZON1050), Link UX360; American Standard AccuLink
S-series communicating/Link furnaces, 5TEM/TAM air handlers, 4TTV/4TWV/4A6V/4A7V/5TTV/5TWV outdoor units

If fault does not clear replace the control Pressing the "Restore Factory Defaults" button will reset all control settings back to the original setting
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Major.

faultCodes.meaning: MULTIPLE ZONE PANEL CONFIGURATION FAULT: Two zone panels are installed and both have the zone panel dipswitch in the same position
checks: Zone Panel for zones 1-4 should be in "Primary" position. Zone Panel for zones 5-8 should be in "Secondary" position. When a Zone Panel is discovered it is created in the equipment list. Depending on the position of the switch the device is categorized as primary or secondary. If the switch position is changed after discovering the original switch position, a second device is created in the equipment list. Now two Zone Panels with the same serial number will be in the equipment list (one will be Online and the other Offline). Navigate to the Diagnostics→Summary Table screen to remove the Offline device.
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Major.
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.4 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: ZONING STATIC PRESSURE CONFIGURATION FAULT: Zoning has been enabled but the differential static pressure sensor has not been enabled
checks: When zoning is enabled the differential static pressure sensor should be automatically enabled; press "Restore Factory Defaults" button to reconfigure this setting Pressing the "Restore Factory Defaults" button will reset all control settings back to the original setting"
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical.

faultCodes.meaning: NO PRIMARY ZONE PANEL CONFIGURATION FAULT: A secondary zone panel has been created with no primary zone panel
checks: Check the position of the Zone Panel switch. At least one Zone Panel switch must be in the "primary" position. When a Zone Panel is discovered it is created in the equipment list. Depending on the position of the switch the device is categorized as primary or secondary. If the switch position is changed after discovering the original switch position, a second device is created in the equipment list. Now two Zone Panels with the same serial number will be in the equipment list (one will be Online and the other Offline). Navigate to the Diagnostics→Summary Table screen to remove the Offline device.
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical.
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.5 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: COMPRESSOR DOME TEMPERATURE SENSOR IMPROPER ATTACHMENT: Compressor temperature sensor must increase by 20 degrees within 6 minutes of startup Depending on compressor type; the sensor may be located on top of compressor dome or discharge line

faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.15 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: DEFROST FAULT B AND/OR C: Defrost Fault B and/or C Very high delta T Defrost terminated at least 10 times in a row on maximum override time (15 minutes) instead of temperature

faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.15 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.15 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: LPCO SOFT LOCKOUT: Low pressure cut-out open (5 minute soft lockout) (Heating) opens at 35 PSI and closes at 55 PSI (Cooling) opens at 50 PSI and closes at 70 PSI
checks: System low on charge Refrigerant restriction Indoor airflow restriction (cooling mode) Outdoor airflow restriction (heating mode) Wiring to low pressure switch either open or shorted
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Normal. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 79.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.15 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: LPCO NOT RESET DURING SOFT LOCKOUT: The low suction pressure switch has not reset within the 5 minute soft lockout period Unit will regain operation once switch closes
checks: System has little to no refrigerant Refrigerant restriction Wiring to low pressure switch is either open or shorted
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Major. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 79.01' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.15 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: LPCO HARD LOCKOUT: Low suction pressure switch has tripped multiple times within a short time period (hard lockout)
checks: System has little to no refrigerant Refrigerant restriction Wiring to low pressure switch is either open or shorted
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 79.02' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.16 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: HIGH PRESSURE TRIP: High pressure switch has tripped (5 minute soft lockout) HPCO opens at 650PSIG and closes below 500 PSIG Multiple occurrences will result in High Pressure Trip Hard Lockout (080.01) and Universal Hard Lockout (184.08) for VSPD system
checks: Cooling Mode - Refrigerant overcharge - Outdoor fan failure - Outdoor airflow restriction Heating Mode - Refrigerant overcharge - Indoor blower failure - Indoor airflow restriction - Non-condensables
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Normal. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 80.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.16 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: HIGH PRESSURE TRIP HARD LOCKOUT: High pressure switch has opened multiple times within a short time period or HPCO switch has not reset within the 5 minute soft lockout period (hard lockout) Universal Hard Lockout (184.08) will accompany this alarm for VSPD system
checks: Cooling Mode - Refrigerant overcharge - Outdoor fan failure - Outdoor airflow restriction Heating Mode - Refrigerant overcharge - Indoor blower failure - Indoor airflow restriction - Non-condensables
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 80.01' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.16 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: REDUCED CAPACITY FROM HIGH PRESSURE TRIP: High Pressure trip point has been exceeded and a 5 minute time out has been enforced Restart is allowed but with reduced capacity
checks: Cooling Mode - Refrigerant overcharge - Outdoor fan failure - Outdoor airflow restriction Heating Mode - Refrigerant overcharge - Indoor blower failure - Indoor airflow restriction - Non-condensables
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Normal. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 80.02' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.16 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: ROLLOUT OPEN: Open flame rollout Furnace will not operate; some furnaces are manual reset
checks: Air impingement on burners or flame Draft inducer not operating properly Restricted heat exchanger Low outlet gas pressure
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 87.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.16 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: GROUND FAULT: Proper earth ground not detected (more than 8v line neutral to ground)
checks: Furnace ground not connected to earth ground Chassis grounds not connected or poor connection Incoming power supply not grounded to main electrical panel
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Normal. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 88.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.16 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: GROUND FAULT: The drive has detected 10 amps of current to ground for 10
checks: Run drive diagnostics and consult Variable Speed Outdoor
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 88.01' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.16 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: EQUIPMENT MISSING: Equipment that was auto discovered at start-up is no longer reporting When communicating systems are initially powered the comfort control will auto discover and remember all equipment reported on the communication bus
checks: Verify voltage between D & B at all communicating components - 12vDC = good communication - 16vDC = loss of communication
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 89.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.17 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: EQUIPMENT NOT RESPONDING TO HEAT/COOL DEMAND: Expected equipment does not respond to the heat/cool demand message
checks: Verify voltage between D & B at all communicating components -12vDC = good communication -16vDC = loss of communication
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 89.01' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.17 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER COMM CRC: Blower motor unrecognized response Communication with blower motor cannot be established
checks: Reboot line voltage to indoor unit and check to see if fault clears If error does not clear contact your local field rep for additional support
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Normal. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 90.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.17 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: INDUCER COMM CRC: Inducer motor unrecognized response Communication with draft inducer motor cannot be established
checks: Reboot line voltage to furnace and check to see if fault clears If error does not clear contact your local field rep for additional support
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Normal. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 90.01' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.17 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: EXCESSIVE COMMUNICATION ERRORS: Excessive bus communication errors (i.e. communication between outdoor/indoor/ thermostat). Comfort control is continually attempting to communicate with no idle detected (bus busy)
checks: D and B wiring reversed at comfort control, outdoor unit or indoor unit If a communicating air cleaner is installed, remove (D) data wire and check to see if fault clears Low and High voltage wire routing. Avoid routing low voltage wiring next to high voltage wiring. If error does not clear contact your local field rep for additional support
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Normal. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 90.02' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.17 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER COMMUNICATION LOSS: (CLII / AccuLink units only) Loss of communication between serial communicating blower motor and control board (3-Stage/Modulating Furnaces only) Corrupted signal between integrated furnace control board and inducer drive control board can also cause this fault
checks: No line voltage to blower motor or inducer motor control board - Furnace 115vAC - Air Handler 230vAC Faulty low voltage connection between control board and blower motor 12vDC should be measured between 12v pin and GND pin on control board and at terminals 1 & 4 at blower motor low voltage plug Perform 24volt “Go/No-Go Test” by applying 24vAC to pins 3 & 4 at blower motor low voltage harness If motor runs replace control board if motor does not run and motor harness tests good, replace motor assembly (3-Stage/Modulating Furnace only) Disconnect 4-pin connector from E9 on furnace control board, cycle power, then test blower operation If blower runs, the inducer drive control board is causing the fault
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 91.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.18 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: INDUCER COMMUNICATION LOSS: Loss of communication between furnace control board and draft inducer motor control board
checks: Faulty connection or harness between furnace control board and draft inducer motor control board On a call for heat the GREEN COM LED on the inducer motor control board should be flashing to confirm communication with furnace control board Faulty inducer drive board
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 91.01' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.18 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: SYSTEM COMMUNICATION ERROR: Loss of heat/cool demand Heat/Cool demand is generated by comfort control every 1 minute and a fault is reported after 3 missed messages
checks: Data line to comfort control broken or disconnected - 0vDC measured between D & B at comfort control with ~12vDC measured at indoor unit Data (D) line and common (B) line reversed at outdoor unit - The Bit Master LED on indoor control board will be off, dim or flickering - 0vDC will be measured with D & B wires connected at outdoor unit - 12vDC will be measured on D & B field wires when disconnected from outdoor unit Data (D) line grounded going to outdoor unit - The Bit Master LED on indoor control board will be off, dim or flickering - 0vDC will be measured with D & B wires connected at outdoor unit - 0vDC will also be measured on D & B field wires when disconnected from outdoor unit If a communicating air cleaner is installed, remove (D) data wire and check to see if fault clears
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 91.02' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.19 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: NO SYSTEM CLOCK: System clock is not reporting System Clock is set by the Bit Master which is part of indoor control board (Air Handler or Furnace Control Board) or Relay Panel
checks: The control is not communicating with the indoor unit or Relay Panel - 12vDC = good communication - 16vDC = loss of communication
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 91.03' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.19 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: COMMUNICATION MIS-WIRE ERROR: Communicating control mis-wire
checks: The (R) wire and (D) wire have been reversed at the comfort control or indoor unit
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 91.05' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.19 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: COMMUNICATION ERROR - LOW BUS VOLTAGE: Communicating bus voltage stuck low
checks: Communicating air cleaner with faulty control board Disconnect air cleaner and check if alert clears. If alert clears, replace control board per service bulletin The (D) wire and (B) wire have been reversed at the comfort control, outdoor unit or indoor unit
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 91.06' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.19 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: CLII MEDIA ACCESS CONTROL CHIP READ (INVALID) REVISION 0: HVAC communication bus did not initialize correctly
checks: A recent reboot of the thermostat did not initialize the internal components completely, causing a loss of communications Power down the thermostat for 5 seconds, then power it back up
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 91.99' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.19 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: CHECK FUSE: 24v fuse on control board is open Status LED will also be “ON” solid when this fault condition exists
checks: Shorted low voltage field wiring High amp draw in low voltage circuit High resistance in field wiring
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 92.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.19 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: EXT GAS VALVE ERROR: Control tried to energize gas valve, but 24v not sensed
checks: Open wiring in gas valve circuit
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 93.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.20 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: EXT GAS VALVE ERROR: Control senses 24v at the gas valve when it should not be present
checks: Shorted wiring in gas valve circuit external to control board Incorrect wiring to gas valve
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 93.01' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.20 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: INT GAS VALVE ERROR: Control board not sensing voltage when voltage should be present
checks: Replace furnace control board
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 93.02' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.20 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: INT GAS VALVE ERROR: Control board sensing voltage when voltage should not be present
checks: Replace furnace control board
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 93.03' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.20 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: Y1 OFF ERROR: Y1 relay on indoor unit control board is “OFF” with a call for cooling If comfort control is setup for single stage cooling and a communicating outdoor unit is not discovered on the communicating bus, the Y1 relay on the indoor control board will apply 24v to Y1 terminal on a active call for cooling
checks: Internal control failure Replace control board
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Major. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 101.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.20 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: Y1 ON ERROR: Y1 relay on indoor unit control board is “ON” without a call for cooling If comfort control is setup for single stage cooling and a communicating outdoor unit is not discovered on the communicating bus, the Y1 relay on the indoor control board will apply 24v to Y1 terminal on a active call for cooling
checks: 24 volts sensed on Y1 terminal of low voltage terminal board without an active call for cooling 24 volts applied to Y1 terminal when a communicating outdoor unit is installed Onboard Y1 relay stuck closed - Replace control board
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Major. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 101.01' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.20 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: Y2 NO Y1: 24 volts detected on Y2 without voltage applied on Y1 at the outdoor unit
checks: Y1 and Y2 field wiring reversed
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Major. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 102.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.20 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: ELECTRIC HEAT RELAY STUCK OPEN: Heat relay on control board is stuck open
checks: Replace control board
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Normal. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 104.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.20 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: ELECTRIC HEAT RELAY STUCK CLOSED: " Voltage is being sensed by onboard sensing circuit when no voltage should be present"
checks: (CLII / AccuLink units only) Disconnect harness from control board to electric heaters and recycle power; if error clears, voltage is being induced on harness or harness wiring by an external source - If error does not clear; replace control board (Hyperion / ForeFront units only) Heater relay failure Open element or non-cycling limit switch (NTCO) open Follow troubleshooting flowchart in heater Service Facts
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Normal. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 104.01' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.21 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: ALL ELECTRIC HEAT RELAYS STUCK OPEN: All heat relays on EHC are stuck open
checks: Replace control board
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 104.02' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.21 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT RELAY INTERLOCK OFF ERROR: Heat interlock relay on control board is stuck open The heater interlock relay is an internal relay which confirms the blower has been energized before allowing the electric heat to energize
checks: Replace control board
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Normal. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 105.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.21 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT RELAY INTERLOCK ON ERROR: Heat interlock relay on control board is stuck closed The heater interlock relay is an internal relay which confirms the blower has been energized before allowing the electric heat to energize
checks: Replace control board
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Normal. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 105.01' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.21 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT RELAY AND HEAT INTERLOCK RELAY ON ERROR: Heat relay and heat interlock relay on indoor unit control board is stuck closed The heater interlock relay is an internal relay which confirms the blower has been energized before allowing the electric heat to energize
checks: Replace control board
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Critical. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 105.02' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.21 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: INDOOR EXTERNAL SWITCH HAS BEEN ACTIVATED: The External Switch configuration has been enabled and external switch contacts are open at the indoor unit
checks: Verify proper external switch configuration at indoor unit. Diagnose the open circuit connected to the external switch terminals.
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Major. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 106.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.21 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: OUTDOOR EXTERNAL SWITCH HAS BEEN ACTIVATED: The External Switch configuration has been enabled and external switch contacts are open at the outdoor unit
checks: Verify proper external switch configuration at outdoor unit. Diagnose the open circuit connected to the external switch terminals
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Normal. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 106.01' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.21 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: HIGH VOLTAGE ARC DETECTED: Air cleaner off due to momentary arc
checks: Dirty collection cells, field charger or prefilter - Clean and retest Wet collection cells, field charger or prefilter - Dry and retest Arcing through field charger plastic frame - Replace field charger
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Normal. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 107.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.22 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: HIGH VOLTAGE ARC SOFT LOCKOUT: Repetitive high voltage arcing detected on the air cleaner (1 hour lockout) If the unit detects 10 consecutive cleaning cycles which were interrupted because of an arc, the unit will go into an 1 hour lockout period
checks: Dirty collection cells, field charger or prefilter - Clean and retest Wet collection cells, field charger or prefilter - Dry and retest Arcing through field charger plastic frame - Replace field charger
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Major. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 107.01' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.22 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: HIGH VOLTAGE OUTPUT TOO HIGH: Air cleaner high voltage output is at least 10% more than selected output voltage (9.6kv, 9.0kv or 8.0kv)
checks: Check for arcing through the collection cells and field charger Check door operation by referring to “Testing the Door” on page 17 of the air cleaner’s Service Facts
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Major. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 108.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.22 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: HIGH VOLTAGE OUTPUT TOO LOW: Air cleaner high voltage output is at least 10% less than selected output voltage (9.6kv, 9.0kv or 8.0kv)
checks: Remove air cleaner power door and check output voltage - If voltage is still less low, replace air cleaner power door - If voltage is correct, check collection cells and field charger
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Major. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 108.01' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.22 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: NO HIGH VOLTAGE OUTPUT: Air cleaner high voltage off when it should be on
checks: Dirty collection cells, field charger or prefilter - Clean and retest Wet collection cells, field charger or prefilter - Dry and retest Arcing through field charger plastic frame - Replace field charger Check the power door operation by referring to “Testing the Power Door” on page 17 of the air cleaner’s Service Facts
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Major. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 108.02' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.22 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: INPUT CURRENT HIGH: Air cleaner Input current too high
checks: Clean collection cells and field charger Check for arcing through the field charger and collection cells
faultCodes.notes: System Alert Guide severity: Major. Shown on the thermostat as 'Err 109.00' (XL824/XL850/XL1050/UX360).
faultCodes.source: Trane System Alert Guide (residential communicating systems, ERR/CFG/SOP alerts), 08/05/2020, p.22 (Possible cause / corrective action column copied into checks)

faultCodes.meaning: INPUT CURRENT LOW: Air cleaner Input current too low
