faultCodes.meaning: The evaporator refrigerant pressure of either circuit has risen above 190 psig. The evaporator water pump relay will be de-energized to stop the pump regardless of why the pump is running. The diagnostic will auto reset and the pump will return to normal control when all of the evaporator pressures fall below 185 psig. The primary purpose is to stop the evaporator water pump and its associated pump heat from causing refrigerant side pressures, close to the evaporator relief valve setting, when the chiller is not running, such as could occur with Evap Water Flow Overdue or Evaporator Water Flow Loss Diagnostics.
faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Chiller. Severity: Immediate. Persistence: NonLatch. Active modes [inactive]: All. Reset level: Remote.

faultCodes.meaning: Either the leaving or the entering water temperature exceeded the high evap water temp limit (TU service menu settable –default 105F (65.55C), range 80F (26.67C)-150F(65.55C) for 15 continuous seconds. The evaporator water pump relay will be de-energized to stop the pump but only if it is running due one of the diagnostics listed on the left. The diagnostic will auto reset and the pump will return to normal control when both the entering and leaving temperatures fall 5°F below the trip setting. The primary purpose is to stop the evaporator water pump and its associated pump heat from causing excessive waterside temperatures and waterside pressures when the chiller is not running but the evap pump is on due to either Evap Water Flow Overdue, Evaporator Water Flow Loss , or Low Evap Temp – Unit Off Diagnostics. This diagnostic will not auto clear solely due to the clearing of the enabling diagnostic.
faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Chiller. Severity: Warning and Special Action. Persistence: NonLatch. Active modes [inactive]: Only effective if either 1) Evap Wtr Flow Overdue, 2) Evap Wtr Flow Loss, or 3) Low Evap Rfgt Temp,- Unit Off, diagnostic is active.. Reset level: Remote.

faultCodes.code: Software Error 1003: Call Trane Service Notes: • The following communication loss diagnostics will not occur unless that input or output is required to be present by the particular configuration and installed options for the chiller. • Communication diagnostics (with the exception of “Excessive Loss of Comm” are named by the Functional name of the input or output that is no longer being heard from by the Main Processor. Many LLIDs, such as the Quad Relay LLID, have more than one functional output associated with it. A comm loss with such a multiple function board, will generate multiple diagnostics. Refer to the Chiller’s wiring diagrams to relate the occurrence of multiple communication diagnostics back to the physical LLID boards that they have been assigned to (bound). • Communication loss diagnostics shall be timed based on action (target status) and not annunciation on the operator display.

diagnosticTips: Before resetting, download active and historic diagnostics (with time stamps) with Tracer TU (BAS-SVU047B-EN) or from the display.

Latch diagnostics need a manual reset; NonLatch diagnostics clear when the condition clears. Reset Level is the lowest level of reset that clears it: 'Remote' can be cleared by a BAS or a local reset, 'Local' only at the chiller.
'x' / 'xA' in a diagnostic name stands for the circuit / compressor (1A, 1B, 2A, 2B).

controls.name: Trane CGAM air-cooled scroll chiller 20-130 t (Symbio controls) diagnostics
controls.description: Diagnostics for CGAM air-cooled scroll chillers 20-130 t with Symbio controls (IOM CG-SVX063D-EN, 08/2025): main processor, sensor failure and communication diagnostics. All 112 rows of the manual's diagnostic table(s) are included (rows that repeat a diagnostic name are merged into one entry; the other row is kept in its notes). Each entry: code = diagnostic name as displayed; meaning = the manual's criteria text (verbatim); notes = affects target, severity, persistence, active modes and reset level as printed. Severity mapping used here: Immediate/Normal shutdown + Latch = lockout, Immediate/Normal + NonLatch = shutdown, Special Action/Mode or Warning = warning, Info = info. Latch = manual reset required; NonLatch = clears when the condition returns to normal. Reset level Local = only a local reset (front panel / Tracer TU) clears it; Remote = local or remote (BAS) reset. Approximate legacy classes: Latch + chiller target ~ MMR, NonLatch + chiller ~ MAR, Latch + circuit ~ CMR, NonLatch + circuit ~ CAR, Warning/Info ~ IFW (interpretation, not a Trane table).

faultCodes.meaning: The leaving water temperature exceeded the high evap water temp setting (TV service menu settable– default 55.0°C (131°F)) for 15 continuous seconds. The evaporator water pump relay will be de-energized to stop the pump, but only if it is running due to one of the diagnostics listed on the left. The diagnostic will auto reset and the pump will return to normal control when the temperature falls 2.778°C (5°F) below the trip setting. The primary purpose is to stop the evaporator water pump and its associated pump heat from causing excessive water-side temperatures and water- side pressures when the unit is not running but the evap pump is on due to either Evaporator Water Flow Overdue, Evaporator Water Flow Lost, or Low Evap Water Temp – Unit Off diagnostics. This diagnostic will not auto clear solely due to the clearing of the enabling diagnostic. *at unit installation, especially reversible units, high evap water temp setting will need to be written. The value should be approximately 65.556°C (150°F) for heat pumps.
faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Chiller. Severity: Info and Special Action. Persistence: NonLatch. Active modes [inactive]: Only effective if either 1) Evaporator Water Flow Overdue, 2) Evaporator Water Flow Lost, 3) Low Evap Water Temp: Unit Off, diagnostic is active.. Reset level: Remote. Table: Main processor diagnostics.
faultCodes.source: IOM: Air-Cooled Scroll Chillers Model CGAM With Symbio Controls 20 to 130 Nominal Tons (60 Hz) (CG-SVX063D-EN), diagnostics table p.102

faultCodes.meaning: The high pressure cutout switch recognized a high pressure.
faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Circuit. Severity: Immediate. Persistence: Latch. Active modes [inactive]: All. Reset level: Local. Table: Main processor diagnostics.
faultCodes.source: IOM: Air-Cooled Scroll Chillers Model CGAM With Symbio Controls 20 to 130 Nominal Tons (60 Hz) (CG-SVX063D-EN), diagnostics table p.102

faultCodes.meaning: Any circuit’s suction pressure has risen above 95% of the high pressure cutout setting. The evaporator water pump relay will be de-energized to stop the pump regardless of why the pump is running. The diagnostic will auto reset and the pump will return to normal control when all circuits’ suction pressures fall below 85% of the high pressure cutout setting. The primary purpose is to stop the evaporator water pump and its associated pump heat from causing refrigerant side pressures close to the relief valve setting when the chiller is not running, such as could occur with Evaporator Water Flow Overdue, Evaporator Water Flow Lost, or Low Evap Water Temp – Unit Off diagnostics. This condition is unlikely unless a discharge isolation valve is installed and closed.
faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Chiller. Severity: Immediate. Persistence: NonLatch. Active modes [inactive]: All. Reset level: Remote. Table: Main processor diagnostics.
faultCodes.source: IOM: Air-Cooled Scroll Chillers Model CGAM With Symbio Controls 20 to 130 Nominal Tons (60 Hz) (CG-SVX063D-EN), diagnostics table p.102

faultCodes.meaning: The entering evaporator water temp fell below the leaving evaporator water temperature by more than 3°F for 100°F- sec while at least one compressor was running. Severity and Persistence depends on the Inverted Water Temp Diagnostic Severity setpoint (Default = Warning/ NonLatching).
faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Chiller. Severity: Warning or Normal. Persistence: NonLatch or Latch. Active modes [inactive]: Any Ckt(s) Energized [No Ckt(s) Energized]. Reset level: Remote. Table: Main processor diagnostics.
faultCodes.source: IOM: Air-Cooled Scroll Chillers Model CGAM With Symbio Controls 20 to 130 Nominal Tons (60 Hz) (CG-SVX063D-EN), diagnostics table p.102

faultCodes.meaning: The leaving evaporator water temp fell below the entering evaporator water temperature by more than 3°F for 100°F- sec. Severity and Persistence depends on the Inverted Water Temp Diagnostic Severity setpoint (Default = Warning/NonLatching). There is a 60 second ignore time after the condition to enable the diagnostic is met. During the ignore time, the temperature error is not integrated.
faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Chiller. Severity: Warning or Normal. Persistence: NonLatch or Latch. Active modes [inactive]: Unit energized and all ckts’ reversing valves in heating direction [Unit deenergized or any ckt’s reversing valve in cooling direction]. Reset level: Remote. Table: Main processor diagnostics.
faultCodes.source: IOM: Air-Cooled Scroll Chillers Model CGAM With Symbio Controls 20 to 130 Nominal Tons (60 Hz) (CG-SVX063D-EN), diagnostics table p.103

faultCodes.meaning: This feature is active on cooling-only units, and heat pumps when in cooling mode. The circuit must have EXV superheat control.

faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Circuit. Severity: Normal. Persistence: Latch. Active modes [inactive]: Ckt Energized [Ckt Not Energized]. Reset level: Local. Table: Main processor diagnostics.

faultCodes.meaning: The leaving chilled water temperature fell below the leaving water temp cutout setting for 30 degree F seconds while the Chiller is in the Stop mode, or in Auto mode with no compressors running. Energize Evap Water pump Relay until diagnostic auto resets, then return to normal evap pump control. Automatic reset occurs when the temp rises 2°F above the cutout setting for 30 minutes. When this diagnostic is active AND Leaving Water Temperature sensor diagnostic (loss of comm or out of range) the Evap Water pump relay shall be de-energized. If evaporator protection temperature sensors are installed, the effect is on the appropriate circuit. Else, the effect is on the chiller.
faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Chiller or Circuit. Severity: Warning and Special Action. Persistence: NonLatch. Active modes [inactive]: Unit in Stop Mode, or in Auto Mode and No Ckt (s) Energized [Any Ckt Energized]. Reset level: Remote. Table: Main processor diagnostics.
faultCodes.source: IOM: Air-Cooled Scroll Chillers Model CGAM With Symbio Controls 20 to 130 Nominal Tons (60 Hz) (CG-SVX063D-EN), diagnostics table p.103

faultCodes.meaning: The evap entering or leaving water temperature fell below the cutout setpoint for 30 degree F Seconds while a compressor was running. Automatic reset occurs when the temperature rises 2 °F above the cutout setting for 2 minutes. This diagnostic shall not deenergize the Evaporator Water Pump Output. If this diagnostic is active the Low Evap Leaving Water Temp: Unit Off diagnostic shall be suppressed. If evaporator protection temperature sensors are installed, the effect is on the appropriate circuit. Else, the effect is on the chiller.
faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Chiller or Circuit. Severity: Immediate and Special Action. Persistence: NonLatch. Active modes [inactive]: Any Ckt[s] Energized [No Ckt(s) Energizd]. Reset level: Remote. Table: Main processor diagnostics.
faultCodes.source: IOM: Air-Cooled Scroll Chillers Model CGAM With Symbio Controls 20 to 130 Nominal Tons (60 Hz) (CG-SVX063D-EN), diagnostics table p.103

faultCodes.meaning: This diagnostic is only effective if all the following requirements are met: 1) Unit is running. 2) THR Control is enabled. 3) THR entering water temperature is less than 4° C, or discharge temperature integral is greater than Discharge Temperature Integral Limit in all the energized circuits. It shall be de-activated when any one of the following requirement is met: 1) THR entering water temperature is greater than 5°C., and the discharge saturated temperature is greater than minimum discharge saturated temperature in at least one energized circuit, see Total Heat Recovery Control Algorithm specification for details. 2) THR entering water temperature is invalid (comm loss or sensor diagnostic). 3) Total Heat Recovery Control disabled. 4) No compressor energized.
faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Heat Recovery. Severity: Warning. Persistence: NonLatch. Active modes [inactive]: Unit energized and THR control enabled [Unit deenergized or THR disabled]. Reset level: Remote. Table: Main processor diagnostics.

faultCodes.meaning: A software monitor has detected a condition in which there was a continuous 1 minute period of compressor operation, with a misaligned statemachine. Reported if state chart misalignment occurred inferred from the Capacity Control, Circuit, or Compressor State Machines being in Stopped state or Inactive state while a compressor was operating and this condition existed for at least 1 minute. The presence of this software error message suggests an internal software problem has been detected. The events that led up to this failure, if known, should be recorded and transmitted to Trane Controls Engineering.

The presence of this software error message suggests an internal software problem has been detected. faultCodes.meaning: The suction temperature measurement is larger than the entering temperature by more than a threshold value for 5 continuous minutes. The threshold value is 3°C (5.4°F) for cooling-only units, and 5°C (9°F) for heat pumps. The entering temperature is the evaporator entering water temperature when the reversing valve is in the cooling direction, and the ambient air temperature when the reversing valve is in the heating direction. There is an ignore time of 2 minutes following circuit startup. The trip criteria is not evaluated (and time above the threshold is not counted) until the ignore time passes.
faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Circuit. Severity: Immediate. Persistence: Latch. Active modes [inactive]: Ckt Energized [Ckt Not Energized]. Reset level: Local. Table: Main processor diagnostics.
faultCodes.source: IOM: Air-Cooled Scroll Chillers Model CGAM With Symbio Controls 20 to 130 Nominal Tons (60 Hz) (CG-SVX063D-EN), diagnostics table p.105

diagnosticTips: Before resetting, download active and historic diagnostics (with time stamps) with Tracer TU (BAS-SVU047B-EN) or from the display.

Latch diagnostics need a manual reset; NonLatch diagnostics clear when the condition clears. Reset Level is the lowest level of reset that clears it: 'Remote' can be cleared by a BAS or a local reset, 'Local' only at the chiller.
'x' / 'xA' in a diagnostic name stands for the circuit / compressor (1A, 1B, 2A, 2B).
Compressor Fault Lockout: the compressor fault switch input stays open more than 35 min, or 5 compressor fault diagnostics occur within 210 min.

controls.name: Trane Ascend ACSA/ACXA air-cooled scroll chiller / heat pump (Symbio 800) diagnostics
controls.description: Diagnostics for Ascend ACS/ACX air-cooled scroll chillers and heat pump chillers 80-230 t with Symbio 800 (IOM AC-SVX004D-EN, 05/2025, Tables 28-30: main processor, sensor failure, communication). The PDF tables are borderless and were rebuilt cell by cell, so re-check any row you rely on against the PDF. All 107 rows of the manual's diagnostic table(s) are included. Each entry: code = diagnostic name as displayed; meaning = the manual's criteria text (verbatim); notes = affects target, severity, persistence, active modes and reset level as printed. Severity mapping used here: Immediate/Normal shutdown + Latch = lockout, Immediate/Normal + NonLatch = shutdown, Special Action/Mode or Warning = warning, Info = info. Latch = manual reset required; NonLatch = clears when the condition returns to normal. Reset level Local = only a local reset (front panel / Tracer TU) clears it; Remote = local or remote (BAS) reset. Approximate legacy classes: Latch + chiller target ~ MMR, NonLatch + chiller ~ MAR, Latch + circuit ~ CMR, NonLatch + circuit ~ CAR, Warning/Info ~ IFW (interpretation, not a Trane table).

faultCodes.meaning: Either the leaving or the entering water temperature exceeded the high evap water temp setting (TU service menu settable – default 40.5°C (105°F)) for 15 continuous seconds. The evaporator water pump relay will be de- energized to stop the pump, but only if it is running due to one of the diagnostics listed on the left. The diagnostic will auto reset and the pump will return to normal control when both the entering and leaving falls 2.778°C (5°F) below the trip setting. The primary purpose is to stop the evaporator water pump and its associated pump heat from causing excessive water-side temperatures and water-side pressures when the unit is not running but the evap pump is on due to either Evaporator Water Flow Overdue, Evaporator Water Flow Lost , or Low Evap Water Temp – Unit Off diagnostics. This diagnostic will not auto clear solely due to the clearing of the enabling diagnostic. *At unit installation, especially reversible units, high evap water temp setting will need to be written. The value should be approximately 65.5°C (150°F) for heat pumps
faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Chiller. Severity: Info and Special Action. Persistence: NonLatch. Active modes [inactive]: Only effective if either 1) Evaporator Water Flow Overdue, 2) Evaporator Water Flow Lost, 3) Low Evap Water Temp: Unit Off, diagnostic is active, 4) Heating mode. Reset level: Remote. Table: Table 28. Main processor diagnostics.
faultCodes.source: IOM: Ascend Air-Cooled Chillers Models ACS and ACX with Symbio 800 controls (AC-SVX004D-EN), diagnostics table p.80

faultCodes.meaning: The high pressure cutout switch recognized a high pressure.

faultCodes.meaning: Any circuit’s suction pressure has risen above 95% of the high pressure cutout setting. The evaporator water pump relay will be de-energized to stop the pump regardless of why the pump is running. The diagnostic will auto reset and the pump will return to normal control when all circuits’ suction pressures fall below 85% of the high pressure cutout setting. The primary purpose is to stop the evaporator water pump and its associated pump heat from causing refrigerant side pressures close to the relief valve setting when the chiller is not running, such as could occur with Evaporator Water Flow Overdue, Evaporator Water Flow Lost, or Low Evap Water Temp – Unit Off diagnostics. This condition is unlikely unless a discharge isolation valve is installed and closed.
faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Chiller. Severity: Immediate. Persistence: NonLatch. Active modes [inactive]: All. Reset level: Remote. Table: Table 28. Main processor diagnostics.
faultCodes.source: IOM: Ascend Air-Cooled Chillers Models ACS and ACX with Symbio 800 controls (AC-SVX004D-EN), diagnostics table p.80

faultCodes.meaning: Not Enabled (Default): diagnostic is Non-Latching and Warning. Enabled: diagnostic is Latching and Normal Shutdown. The entering evaporator water temp fell below the leaving evaporator water temperature by more than 3°F for 100° F-sec while at least one compressor was running. Diagnostic will auto clear if the leaving water temp – entering water temp < 3°F. It can warn of improper flow direction through the evaporator, misbound water temperature sensors, improper sensor installation, partially failed sensors, or other system problems. Note that either entering or leaving water temp sensor or the water system could be at fault.
faultCodes.notes: Affects target: Chiller. Severity: Warning/Normal. Persistence: NonLatch/Latch. Active modes [inactive]: Any Ckt(s) Energized [No Ckt(s) Energized]. Reset level: Remote. Table: Table 28. Main processor diagnostics.

faultCodes.meaning: Not Enabled (Default): diagnostic is Non-Latching and Warning. Enabled: diagnostic is Latching and Normal Shutdown. The leaving evaporator water temp fell below the entering evaporator water temperature by more than 3°F for 100° F-sec. There is a 60 second ignore time after the condition to enable the diagnostic is met. During the ignore time, the temperature error is not integrated. Diagnostic will auto clear if the entering water temp – leaving water temp < 3F. It can warn of improper flow direction through the evaporator, misbound water temperature sensors, improper sensor installation, partially failed sensors, or other system problems. Note that either entering or leaving water temp sensor or the water system could be at fault.

faultCodes.meaning: This feature is factory enabled for glycol applications only. The diagnostic occurs if the EXV (normal cooling mode only) is consistently and significantly more open than internal models predict for the conditions. This would occur with lack of subcooling from the condenser, a condition that generally suggests undercharging or charge loss. Pressure sensor errors or excessive compressor capacity over the commanded capacity could also cause this diagnostic. (Adjustment is available to mitigate nuisance tripping)

faultCodes.meaning: The suction temperature measurement is larger than the entering temperature by more than a threshold value for 5 continuous minutes. The threshold value is 4°C (7.2°F) for cooling-only units, and 20°C for heat pumps. The entering temperature is the evaporator entering water temperature when the reversing valve is in the cooling direction, and the ambient air temperature when the reversing valve is in the heating direction. There is an ignore time of 2 minutes following circuit start-up. The trip criteria is not evaluated (and time above the threshold is not counted) until the ignore time passes.

diagnosticTips: Before resetting, download active and historic diagnostics (with time stamps) with Tracer TU (BAS-SVU047B-EN) or from the display.

Latch diagnostics need a manual reset; NonLatch diagnostics clear when the condition clears. Reset Level is the lowest level of reset that clears it: 'Remote' can be cleared by a BAS or a local reset, 'Local' only at the chiller.
'x' / 'xA' in a diagnostic name stands for the circuit / compressor (1A, 1B, 2A, 2B).
Compressor Fault Lockout: the compressor fault switch input stays open more than 35 min, or 5 compressor fault diagnostics occur within 210 min.

controls.name: Trane UCM-CLD chiller control (RTWA / RTWB / RTRA / RTAD) fault codes
controls.description: Legacy UCM-CLD chiller control: the display shows 'Fault <hex code>' plus a default description. Types: MMR = machine shutdown manual reset (lockout), MAR = machine shutdown automatic reset (shutdown), CMR = circuit shutdown manual reset (lockout), CAR = circuit shutdown automatic reset (shutdown), IFW = informational warning (info); priority MMR > MAR > CMR > CAR > IFW. Communication failure codes (4xx) have no type in the manual. The red LED next to the display flashes on CMR or MMR. Text is as printed (including the manual's typos). All 140 codes are included.
appliesTo: RTWA, RTWB (incl. heat pump), RTRA, RTAD with UCM-CLD

controls.name: Trane Tracer SC system controller (LEDs and 7-segment display)
controls.description: Tracer SC building system controller: Status, link, LonTalk, IMC and Ethernet LEDs and the 7-segment boot/status codes (BAS-SVX31U-EN Table 9, PDF pp.136-137). Fault-type 7-segment codes (flashing/solid red status LED, persistent 8 or 5) are listed as fault codes; normal boot, update and status indications are ledPatterns. Flashing red status LED with 'F' + code = fatal error (service required); with 'H' + code = hardware failure. A separate Tracer SC+ table was not obtained (SC+ shares firmware/addressing with Symbio 800).

faultCodes.meaning: Processor in reset, or no functioning software. A persistent “8” means that service is required.
faultCodes.notes: Status LED: Green. Shown on the Tracer SC 7-segment display.
faultCodes.source: Tracer SC IOM (BAS-SVX31U-EN), 7-segment codes, p.136

faultCodes.meaning: Entering operating system. A persistent “5” means the operating system is malfunctioning.
faultCodes.notes: Status LED: Green. Shown on the Tracer SC 7-segment display.
faultCodes.source: Tracer SC IOM (BAS-SVX31U-EN), 7-segment codes, p.137

faultCodes.meaning: Mismatch between level 1 boot loader and hardware. Service is required.
faultCodes.notes: Status LED: Flashing Red. Shown on the Tracer SC 7-segment display.
faultCodes.source: Tracer SC IOM (BAS-SVX31U-EN), 7-segment codes, p.137

faultCodes.meaning: Hardware failure. SC will probably need to be replaced.
faultCodes.notes: Status LED: Flashing Red. Shown on the Tracer SC 7-segment display.
faultCodes.source: Tracer SC IOM (BAS-SVX31U-EN), 7-segment codes, p.137

faultCodes.meaning: Missing level 2 boot loader.
faultCodes.notes: Status LED: Flashing Red. Shown on the Tracer SC 7-segment display.
faultCodes.source: Tracer SC IOM (BAS-SVX31U-EN), 7-segment codes, p.137

faultCodes.meaning: Mismatch between level 2 boot loader and hardware.
faultCodes.notes: Status LED: Flashing Red. Shown on the Tracer SC 7-segment display.
faultCodes.source: Tracer SC IOM (BAS-SVX31U-EN), 7-segment codes, p.137

faultCodes.meaning: Main program is delayed due to multiple crashes (may take up to 4 hours).
faultCodes.notes: Status LED: Flashing Red. Shown on the Tracer SC 7-segment display.
faultCodes.source: Tracer SC IOM (BAS-SVX31U-EN), 7-segment codes, p.137

faultCodes.meaning: Cannot load operating system. May be remedied by SD-card update with appropriate software version.
faultCodes.notes: Status LED: Red. Shown on the Tracer SC 7-segment display.
faultCodes.source: Tracer SC IOM (BAS-SVX31U-EN), 7-segment codes, p.137

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC Status LED: On steady (green)
ledPatterns.meaning: Power reception (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC Status LED: Flashing (red), and an “F” appears on the 7-segment display followed by a code
ledPatterns.meaning: Fatal error. Service required. (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC Status LED: Flashing (red), and an “H” appears on the 7-segment display followed by a code
ledPatterns.meaning: Hardware failure. SC will probably need to be replaced. (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC Link 1 communication LED: L1 TX flickers (green)
ledPatterns.meaning: Data transmission (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC Link 1 communication LED: L1 RX flickers (yellow)
ledPatterns.meaning: Data reception (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC Link 2 communication LED: L2 TX flickers (green)
ledPatterns.meaning: Data transmission (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC Link 2 communication LED: L2 RX flickers (yellow)
ledPatterns.meaning: Data reception (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC LonTalk communication LED: Lon TX flickers (green)
ledPatterns.meaning: Data transmission (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC LonTalk communication LED: Lon RX flickers (yellow)
ledPatterns.meaning: Data reception (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC LonTalk service LED: On steady (red)
ledPatterns.meaning: LonTalk service pin has been pressed: • Short press-broadcast neuron ID and program ID identifies itself so Rover can assign it a DSN. • Long press (more than 15 sec.)-Forces the SC LON node to an unconfigured state and disables LonTalk until reconfigured with Rover. (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC /O/O/ [EIA-232 serial connection] LED: IOIOI TX (green)
ledPatterns.meaning: Data transmission (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC /O/O/ [EIA-232 serial connection] LED: IOIOIO RX (yellow)
ledPatterns.meaning: Data reception (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC IMC LED: IMC TX (green)
ledPatterns.meaning: Data transmission (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC IMC LED: IMC RX (yellow)
ledPatterns.meaning: Data reception (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC Ethernet 1, Ethernet 2 LED: LINK on steady (green)
ledPatterns.meaning: Valid Ethernet connection (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC Ethernet 1, Ethernet 2 LED: ACT flickers (yellow)
ledPatterns.meaning: Data transmission and reception (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC 7-segment '7' with green status LED
ledPatterns.meaning: Starting level 1 boot loader (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC 7-segment '9' with green status LED
ledPatterns.meaning: Starting level 2 boot loader (p.136)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC 7-segment '4 (this number remains for a few seconds)' with green status LED
ledPatterns.meaning: Booting operating system. (p.137)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC 7-segment '-L' with green status LED
ledPatterns.meaning: Loading and initializing main program. (p.137)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC 7-segment '“Dancing dash” dashes flash one at a time: top, middle, bottom' with green status LED
ledPatterns.meaning: Normal operation (p.137)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC 7-segment '3, -, 2, -, 1, - (sequence repeats)' with green status LED
ledPatterns.meaning: Power button was pressed and Tracer SC is shutting down. May take 10 or more seconds. (p.137)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC 7-segment '3, 2, 1 (sequence repeats)' with green status LED
ledPatterns.meaning: Main program shutting down due to reboot command. In most cases, the main program will be restarted. (p.137)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC 7-segment 'Single digit during operation' with green status LED
ledPatterns.meaning: Rotary switch was changed. The new setting of the changed switch is displayed on the 7-segment LED for several seconds. (p.137)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC 7-segment 'U, P, d'
ledPatterns.meaning: Firmware update is in progress. (p.137)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC 7-segment 'd, o, n, E'
ledPatterns.meaning: Updating of the operating system is finished. The Tracer SC can be powered off, the SD card removed, and the Tracer SC restarted. (p.137)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC 7-segment 'F, o, r, C, E'
ledPatterns.meaning: Rotary switches set to 999; forced return to factory defaults in progress. (p.137)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC 7-segment 'C, L, E, A, r'
ledPatterns.meaning: Tracer SC is restoring factory defaults (whether by force return, UI command, or at the beginning of a database restore operation). (p.137)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC 7-segment 'r'
ledPatterns.meaning: Database restore in progress. (p.137)

ledPatterns.pattern: Tracer SC 7-segment 'U' with flashing green status LED
ledPatterns.meaning: Power button was pressed when main program was not running/not responsive. SC is shutting down; wait for LEDs to turn off. (p.137)

diagnosticTips: Dancing dashes on the 7-segment display = normal operation.
Rotary switches set to 999 = forced return to factory defaults ('F, o, r, C, E' then 'C, L, E, A, r').
'H, O, L, d' = main program delayed because of multiple crashes (may take up to 4 h); contact tech support if it repeats.
Red 'F' = cannot load operating system; may be remedied by an SD-card update with the appropriate software version.

controls.name: Trane UC600 programmable controller LEDs
controls.description: UC600 programmable controller LED table (BAS-SVX45K-EN Table 5, PDF p.33). Power-up sequence: red, then flashing green, then solid green. Abnormal indications (power LED solid/blinking red, RX solid yellow = reverse polarity, comm LED not lit) are fault codes; normal indications are ledPatterns.

faultCodes.meaning: Low voltage or malfunction
faultCodes.source: UC600 IOM (BAS-SVX45K-EN), Table 5 LED descriptions, p.33

faultCodes.meaning: Alarm or fault is present (*see note)
faultCodes.source: UC600 IOM (BAS-SVX45K-EN), Table 5 LED descriptions, p.33

faultCodes.code: UC600 Communication (Link, MBUS, IMC) LED RX on solid (yellow)
faultCodes.meaning: Reverse polarity is present
faultCodes.source: UC600 IOM (BAS-SVX45K-EN), Table 5 LED descriptions, p.33

faultCodes.code: UC600 Communication (Link, MBUS, IMC) LED LED not illuminated
faultCodes.meaning: The controller is not detecting communication
checks: • Cycle the power to reestablish communication. • Verify that the controller is capable of communicating with other devices on the link. • Check polarity and baud rate.
faultCodes.source: UC600 IOM (BAS-SVX45K-EN), Table 5 LED descriptions, p.33

ledPatterns.pattern: UC600 Power LED: Solid green
ledPatterns.meaning: Normal operation (Sequence on power-up: Illuminates red, then flashes green, then solid green.) (p.33)

ledPatterns.pattern: UC600 Communication (Link, MBUS, IMC) LED: TX (transmit) blinks green
ledPatterns.meaning: Normal operation; blinks at a fixed rate when transferring data to other devices on the link (TX LED: Regardless of connectivity, the TX will blink as it searches for devices to communicate with.) (p.33)

ledPatterns.pattern: UC600 Communication (Link, MBUS, IMC) LED: RX (receive) blinks yellow
ledPatterns.meaning: Normal operation; blinks at a fixed rate when receiving data from other devices on the link (p.33)

ledPatterns.pattern: UC600 Service LED: Solid green
ledPatterns.meaning: LED has been pressed and remains on until powered down (does not affect normal operation) (p.33)

ledPatterns.pattern: UC600 Service LED: LED not illuminated
ledPatterns.meaning: Normal operation (p.33)

ledPatterns.pattern: UC600 Binary outputs (BO1 through BO4) LED: Solid yellow
ledPatterns.meaning: Relay coil energized (p.33)

ledPatterns.pattern: UC600 Binary outputs (BO1 through BO4) LED: LED not illuminated
ledPatterns.meaning: Relay coil de-energized or No command (p.33)

ledPatterns.pattern: UC600 Ethernet LED: LINK on solid (green)
ledPatterns.meaning: Valid Ethernet connection (p.33)

ledPatterns.pattern: UC600 Ethernet LED: ACT flickers (yellow)
ledPatterns.meaning: Data transmission and reception (p.33)

diagnosticTips: Power LED solid red = low voltage or malfunction: measure 24 VAC and cycle power.
RX LED solid yellow = reversed polarity on the BACnet MS/TP link.
The TX LED blinks regardless of connectivity as it searches for devices; use RX to judge whether anything is answering.

controls.name: Trane Symbio 400-B / Symbio 500 controller on water-source heat pumps (diagnostics, Marquee LED codes)
controls.description: Symbio 400-B/500 unit controller on Trane water-source heat pumps (BAS-SVX092D-EN Tables 10, 11, 18, 20): controller diagnostics with unit response, latching and reset rules; Marquee LED red blink codes (boot/firmware failures) as fault codes; green blink codes and the LED table as ledPatterns. The same controller on blower coils / fan coils / unit ventilators is covered by BAS-SVX093B-EN. All rows of the diagnostic and Marquee tables are included.
appliesTo: Axiom GEH/GEV and other Trane WSHP with Symbio 400-B/500

faultCodes.meaning: High/Low Pressure Cutout/Freeze Protection Unit response: • Fan OFF • Valves Closed • Compressor OFF Note: In a 2-compressor unit, the unit continues to operate if a compressor is available.
faultCodes.notes: Latching. Reset: Auto-reset once every 24 hours. If safety generate a diagnostic more than once, a communicated or manual reset is required.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), controller diagnostics, p.59

faultCodes.meaning: This diagnostic is generated when a fan status device is present and fails to close after one minute of unit startup, or when it opens for more than one minute during normal unit operation. Unit response: • Fan OFF • Valves Closed • Compressor OFF
faultCodes.notes: Latching. Reset: Communicated or manual reset is required.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), controller diagnostics, p.59

faultCodes.meaning: If space temperature is invalid or not present, a space temperature alarm occurs. Unit response: • Fan OFF • Valves Closed • Compressor OFF
faultCodes.notes: Non-latching. Reset: Auto resets.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), controller diagnostics, p.59

faultCodes.meaning: If the Entering Water Temperature is configured but invalid or not present, an entering water temperature alarm occurs. Unit response: • Fan Enabled • No Boiler Control Disabled • Waterside Economizer Enabled
faultCodes.notes: Non-latching. Reset: Auto resets.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), controller diagnostics, p.59

faultCodes.meaning: When the discharge air exceeds the low limit setpoint and the unit cannot correct it by altering capacity, a Discharge Air Temp Low Limit diagnostic is generated. Unit response: • Fan on • Waterside Economizer enabled • compressor disabled
faultCodes.notes: Non-latching. Reset: Auto-reset once every 24 hours. If safety generate a diagnostic more than once, a communicated or manual reset is required.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), controller diagnostics, p.59

faultCodes.meaning: If RH is configured but invalid or not present, a humidity input alarm occurs. Unit response: • Fan Enabled • Valves Enabled • Compressor Enabled • Reheat Disabled
faultCodes.notes: Non-latching. Reset: Auto resets.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), controller diagnostics, p.59

faultCodes.meaning: If CO2 is configured but invalid or not present, a CO2 input alarm occurs. Unit response: • Fan Enabled • Valves Enabled • Compressor Enabled
faultCodes.notes: Non-latching. Reset: Auto resets.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), controller diagnostics, p.59

faultCodes.meaning: The Filter Change Required diagnostic is generated when the fan run-time exceeds the configured limit. This diagnostic is useful for filter change notification. Note: If power to the unit is cycled or discontinued for any reason, all maintenance timers automatically reset. Unit response: • Fan Enabled • Valves Enabled • Compressor Enabled
faultCodes.notes: Non-latching. Reset: Communicated or manual reset is required
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), controller diagnostics, p.60

faultCodes.meaning: If the hard wired fan mode input to the Symbio 400-B/500 controller is invalid, a local fan mode alarm is generated. Unit response: • Fan Enabled • Valves Enabled • Compressor Enabled
faultCodes.notes: Non-latching. Reset: Auto resets.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), controller diagnostics, p.60

faultCodes.meaning: If the hard wired setpoint input to the Symbio 400-B/500 controller is invalid, a local setpoint alarm is generated. Unit response: • Fan Enabled • Valves Enabled • Compressor Enabled
faultCodes.notes: Non-latching. Reset: Auto resets.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), controller diagnostics, p.60

faultCodes.meaning: RefrigLeakDetectionInput = Active Unit response: • Fan High • Compressor OFF • Isolation Valve OFF • Rev Valve Enabled • OAD Enabled • EH/Gas OFF • WSE Closed
faultCodes.notes: Non-latching. Reset: Mitigation Action Requirements: The following mitigation actions must be completed in not more than 15 seconds after the initiation of the output signal of section 7.6.2.4(g), and must be maintained for at least 5 minutes after the output signal has reset.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), controller diagnostics, p.60

faultCodes.meaning: (BV/19) System will operate in the fan-only mode. When fan is at high speed, all other outputs will be disabled. Unit response: • Fan High • Compressor OFF • Isolation Valve OFF • Rev Valve Enabled • OAD Enabled • EH/Gas OFF • WSE Closed
faultCodes.notes: Non-latching. Reset: Auto resets: UL 60335-2-40; ducted HVAC systems that have more than 3.91 lbs. of A2L refrigerant charge will be required to include one or more refrigerant detection sensors - the sensor shall have a 5 minute minimum timer before a reset is allowed.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), controller diagnostics, p.60

faultCodes.meaning: The defrost stat used with the Symbio 400-B/500 controller on DX units is wired in series with the condensing unit. When it opens to indicate a frost condition, the controller senses the open circuit and then de-energizes the compressor output. A defrosting diagnostic is generated at this point.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), controller diagnostics, p.60

faultCodes.code: Symbio 400-B/500 Marquee LED Shows solid red when the unit is powered, but represents low power or a malfunction
faultCodes.meaning: • If low power; could be under voltage or the microprocessor has malfunction. Follow the troubleshoot procedure “24 Vac Measurement,” p. 46 to measure for the expected value range. In addition, see Table 4, p. 24, for a list of 24 Vac draws. • If malfunction; un-power and then re-power unit to bring the unit back up to normal operation.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), LED table, p.44

faultCodes.code: Symbio 400-B/500 Marquee LED Shows blinking red when an alarm or fault exists
faultCodes.meaning: An alarm or fault condition will occur if the value for a given point is invalid or outside the configured limits for the point. Alarm and fault conditions vary, and they can be configured by the programmer.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), LED table, p.44

faultCodes.meaning: Load Field Fail: Attempted load of the field kernel or device tree failed.
checks: 1. Thumb drive with .scfx file, power down, set address rotaries to 991, and power up.
2. Replace controller.
faultCodes.notes: Marquee LED red blink code (blink count) shown during boot / firmware update.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), Marquee LED codes, p.46

faultCodes.meaning: Load Recovery Fail: Attempted load of the recovery image failed.
checks: Replace controller
faultCodes.notes: Marquee LED red blink code (blink count) shown during boot / firmware update.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), Marquee LED codes, p.46

faultCodes.meaning: Field Mount Fail: Failed to mount the field partition during a firmware update attempt.
checks: 1. Thumb drive with .scfx file, power down, set address rotaries to 991, and power up.
2. Replace controller.
faultCodes.notes: Marquee LED red blink code (blink count) shown during boot / firmware update.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), Marquee LED codes, p.46

faultCodes.meaning: Bad Switch Setting: Rotary switches are set to a bad/unknown value.
checks: Contact technical support.
faultCodes.notes: Marquee LED red blink code (blink count) shown during boot / firmware update.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), Marquee LED codes, p.46

faultCodes.meaning: Bad Firmware File: Unable to mount the firmware update file.
checks: Download firmware file again and retry download.
faultCodes.notes: Marquee LED red blink code (blink count) shown during boot / firmware update.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), Marquee LED codes, p.46

faultCodes.meaning: Firmware Not Compatible: Firmware file downloaded is not compatible with this hardware.
checks: Download the correct FW file for the controller.
faultCodes.notes: Marquee LED red blink code (blink count) shown during boot / firmware update.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), Marquee LED codes, p.46

faultCodes.meaning: Field Format Fail: Failed to reformat the field file system.
checks: Replace controller.
faultCodes.notes: Marquee LED red blink code (blink count) shown during boot / firmware update.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), Marquee LED codes, p.46

faultCodes.code: Marquee red 25 Field Attach UBI Fail
faultCodes.meaning: Field Attach UBI Fail: Failed to attach (UBI) to the field file system.
checks: Replace controller.
faultCodes.notes: Marquee LED red blink code (blink count) shown during boot / firmware update.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), Marquee LED codes, p.46

faultCodes.meaning: Field Mount Fail: Failed to mount the field file system.
checks: Replace controller.
faultCodes.notes: Marquee LED red blink code (blink count) shown during boot / firmware update.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), Marquee LED codes, p.46

faultCodes.meaning: Bad Update Method: Don’t know what our update method is.
checks: Contact technical support.
faultCodes.notes: Marquee LED red blink code (blink count) shown during boot / firmware update.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), Marquee LED codes, p.46

faultCodes.code: Marquee red 31 No Firmware File Found
faultCodes.meaning: No Firmware File Found: Unable to find a firmware update file.
checks: Thumb drive has no .scfx file. .scfx file must be located at the root of the USB drive.
faultCodes.notes: Marquee LED red blink code (blink count) shown during boot / firmware update.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), Marquee LED codes, p.46

faultCodes.meaning: Multiple Firmware Found: Multiple firmware update files were found.
checks: Too many .scfx files on the thumb drive. Can only have on .scfx file and must be located in the root of the USB drive.
faultCodes.notes: Marquee LED red blink code (blink count) shown during boot / firmware update.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), Marquee LED codes, p.46

faultCodes.meaning: Firmware Invalid
checks: Download the firmware file again and retry download.
faultCodes.notes: Marquee LED red blink code (blink count) shown during boot / firmware update.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), Marquee LED codes, p.46

faultCodes.meaning: Firmware Invalid
checks: Download the correct FW file again and retry download.
faultCodes.notes: Marquee LED red blink code (blink count) shown during boot / firmware update.
faultCodes.source: Symbio 400-B/500 for water-source heat pumps IOM (BAS-SVX092D-EN), Marquee LED codes, p.46

faultCodes.meaning: Bad Firmware File: Unable to mount the firmware update file.

diagnosticTips: High/Low Pressure Cutout/Freeze Protection is latching: it auto-resets once every 24 h; if the safety trips more than once, a communicated or manual reset is required.
After power-up the controller waits a random 5-30 s before running the unit (random start, not a fault).
Marquee LED solid red = low power or malfunction: measure 24 VAC (troubleshooting procedure '24 Vac Measurement'); LED off = no power or failed controller.
RX LED solid yellow = reverse polarity on the link.
Factory reset: address rotaries 9-9-9 (30 s window shown as Marquee code 45).
Firmware recovery: USB thumb drive with exactly one .scfx file in its root, set rotaries to 991, power up (codes 31/32 = no file / more than one file).

Refrigerant leak detection (A2L units): fan to high, compressor off, isolation valve off; non-latching. Possible causes when unexpected: faulty sensor, IMC comm to the BI LLID, wiring, other gas present (A2L/CO2).

faultCodes.code: Diagnostic: Compressor (1-4) Discharge Pressure Sensor Failure (In Alarm)
faultCodes.meaning: The Pressure sensor is calculated to be in fault and the unit has locked out the compressor from operation. Action: Compressor will be locked out and prevented from running until this diagnostic is cleared.
likelyCauses: Sensor has lost its 5 Vdc Source Signal. Verify that the sensor has 5 Vdc.
Sensor is not wired properly: Verify wiring to the XM Module.
XM Module is not communicating. Confirm the XM Module is up and talking to the Symbio 500.
System has no charge: Verify that the system has a refrigerant charge.
Sensor has failed.
checks: Reset: Manual Reset required once the sensor is in a Normal State. User must toggle the Compressor (1-4) Failure Reset.
faultCodes.notes: Notification class: HVAC Critical Alarm.
faultCodes.source: SCWM IOM (PKG-SVX030B-EN, 11/2025), Tables 38-41 alarms, p.97

faultCodes.code: Diagnostic: Compressor (1-4) Discharge Pressure Sensor Failure (In Fault)
faultCodes.meaning: The Pressure sensor is reading either Above or Below its minimum value, resulting in a Fault Condition after 3 point updates. Action: Compressor will be locked out and prevented from running until this sensor is in a normal state.
likelyCauses: Sensor has lost its 5 Vdc Source Signal. Verify that the sensor has 5 Vdc.
Sensor is not wired properly: Verify wiring to the XM Module.
XM Module is not communicating. Confirm the XM Module is up and talking to the Symbio 500. System has no charge: Verify that the system has a refrigerant charge.
Sensor has failed.
checks: Reset: None, fault clears once sensor is in a normal state.
faultCodes.notes: Notification class: HVAC Critical Alarm.
faultCodes.source: SCWM IOM (PKG-SVX030B-EN, 11/2025), Tables 38-41 alarms, p.97

diagnosticTips: Frostat = saturated suction below 32 F for 5 min (critical, compressor locked out); Frostat limit warning below 36 F limits compressor speed.
High superheat alarm: above 25 F for 10 min; low superheat: below 4 F for 5 min.
Condenser water low-temperature lockout: entering or leaving condenser water below 35 F for 10 min.
Pressure/temperature sensor alarms: check the 5 Vdc sensor supply, the wiring to the XM module and that the XM module communicates with the Symbio controller; thermistors should read about 8-12 kohm.
Manual-reset alarms are cleared by toggling the matching reset point (Compressor (1-4) Failure Reset, Supply Failure Reset, Alarm Reset, Filter Alarm Reset).

controls.name: Trane VRF GMV DC inverter (TRN- models; Gree-built platform) error codes
controls.description: Trane's current VRF line (Trane 'GMV' / Multi Variable heat recovery and heat pump DC inverter VRF, model prefix TRN-, e.g. TRN-VQ72WTAW / TRN-VQ96WTAW / TRN-VQ120WTAW outdoor units, TRN-IC07S1A1 cassettes) is built by Gree: the Trane IOM directs users to a 'Gree authorized maintenance center', and the codes are the Gree GMV-family codes. It is NOT the older Trane / Mitsubishi Electric CITY MULTI line (Mitsubishi 4-digit codes do not apply). Code groups: L*, d*, y*, o* = indoor unit; E* = outdoor protection; F*, b* = outdoor sensors; J* = outdoor system protection; P* = compressor inverter drive; H* = fan inverter drive; G* = grid-connection / PV drive; U* = debugging; C* = communication / addressing / configuration; A*, n*, q* = status and settings, not faults. All 261 codes of IOM section 7.2 are included; the IOM gives no causes, checks or severity (it refers to the Gree 'engineering debugging and after-sales maintenance manual of DC inverter VRF unit', not public).

Combustion air pressure switch (proves the combustion fan motor CFM)
Frostat (evaporator freeze protection, on RTOM/RTRM input)
Smoke detector and condensate overflow switch inputs (RTOM) — shut the unit down
Fan proving switch and dirty filter switch (RTOM) — produce fan-failure / service diagnostics

terminalLabels.R: 24 VAC hot to thermostat (conventional-thermostat interface on LTB)
terminalLabels.X2: Trane thermostat interface terminal (system-failure / emergency-heat indication on some units) — verify on the unit diagram
terminalLabels.TEST 1 / TEST 2: Short 2-3 s to enter ReliaTel/UCP test mode
terminalLabels.ZSM 1-12: Zone sensor module terminals (zone temp, setpoint, mode, fan, LEDs) numbered on the LTB per the unit diagram
terminalLabels.BAS: RTCI/TCI communication module terminals (Trane Comm 3/4, BACnet MS/TP + / -); Symbio 700 BACnet MS/TP on the controller

sequenceOfOperation: Cooling (ReliaTel): on Y1/zone-sensor cooling demand the RTRM starts the IDM (immediately or per fan mode), then — if an RTEM economizer is fitted and outdoor conditions are suitable — modulates the economizer first; when the economizer cannot satisfy the load, the RTRM closes CC1 to start CPR1 (and ODM) after the minimum off-timer; Y2 / further demand brings on CPR2 via CC2. HPC/LPC trips are counted per cooling cycle; repeated trips lock out that compressor until reset.

Heating (gas, ReliaTel): on W1 the RTRM energizes the ignition control (IGN); the combustion fan motor (CFM) starts and the pressure switch must prove; after prepurge the direct spark igniter (DS1) sparks and the gas valve (GV) opens; the flame sensor must prove within the trial time or IGN retries then locks out (heat-failure diagnostic). Indoor fan starts after the heat fan-on delay; TCO limits open the ignition circuit on overtemperature. W2 stages the second heat stage / high fire.
Heat pump: RTRM energizes the reversing valve solenoid in the cooling mode (Trane 'O' logic), defrost by demand/time via the defrost control; electric heat staged via W1/W2 with the compressor.

Ventilation / economizer: RTEM drives the economizer actuator to minimum position when the fan runs occupied; free cooling enabled by dry-bulb or enthalpy (OHS) comparison; CO2 demand-controlled ventilation via RTVM when fitted.
notes: Designators CPR, CC, ODM, IDM, TNS, HPC, LPC are transcribed from the legend of Trane wiring diagram 1213-4333 (Trane eLibrary); CFM, DS1 and GV from the legends of 1213-4803A_02142024 / 12134731_B_08302023 (current Precedent gas/electric). The remaining designators are corroborated only by help-center text or are builder memory (marked UNVERIFIED) and must be confirmed against the diagram printed on the unit (drawing number on the control-box door). FS, PS, SMD, CCH and F1/F2 were removed pending a legend read. Family confidence is LOW until the 1213-4333 legend has been read in full.

3-phase scroll compressors on 208-230/460/575 V units are rotation-sensitive: verify rotation at start-up (suction/discharge pressures, noise); Trane fits a phase monitor on many 3-phase ReliaTel/Symbio units — check for a 'PM' / phase-monitor relay on the diagram before assuming.

Symbio 700 units: the controller replaces RTRM/RTOM/RTEM functions on one board with expansion modules; thermostat interface is via the Symbio 700 low-voltage terminals (R/G/Y1/Y2/W1/W2) or zone sensor; BACnet MS/TP directly on the controller.

commonIssues.symptom: RTRM System LED2 flashing 2 times every 2 s; unit running but zone complains
likelyCauses: Zone temperature sensor wiring open/shorted (10k thermistor) — very common
Programmable zone sensor communication failure
Supply fan proving / dirty filter input
Compressor lockout from HPC/LPC trips
checks: Ohm the ZTS at the LTB (about 10 kohm at 77 F)
Read the specific diagnostic through zone sensor LEDs / test mode / service tool
Check fan proving and filter switches and their tubing

commonIssues.symptom: Economizer stuck open or closed, high humidity / high supply temperature, RTEM LED flashing
likelyCauses: Failed RTEM module or economizer actuator
Mixed-air or outdoor-air sensor drifted/open
Enthalpy (OHS) sensor failure
Linkage / damper blades seized
checks: Run test mode to the economizer step and watch actuator travel
Check MAS/OAS resistance and the RTEM flash code
Verify minimum position setpoint and the OA changeover setting

commonIssues.symptom: No cooling, Cool LED flashing / compressor locked out
likelyCauses: Low charge from leaks (LPC trips)
Dirty condenser or failed ODM (HPC trips)
Compressor contactor or internal overload
Phase loss or reverse rotation on 3-phase scroll
checks: Pressures and superheat/subcooling per circuit
ODM operation and condenser cleanliness
CC coil voltage and contacts, compressor amps vs RLA
Reset by cycling 24 V power and observe the next trip
sources: https://support.trane.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037864091 (Trane Commercial Help Center — Why is the red light on the phase monitor on? — reverse rotation / phase loss)

commonIssues.symptom: Gas heat will not light or locks out intermittently (Heat LED flashing)
likelyCauses: Dirty/cracked flame sensor rod (low microamps)
Combustion pressure switch not closing (blocked flue/inducer, cracked tubing)
Gas pressure low / regulator
Igniter failed
High-limit TCO tripping on low airflow (dirty filters, belt slip)
checks: Watch a full ignition trial in test mode heat step
Flame current, manifold pressure, pressure-switch differential
Filters, belt tension and blower amps
sources: Builder field-pattern summary; ignition sequence per ReliaTel gas/electric IOM RT-SVX21

commonIssues.symptom: Supply fan failure diagnostic (Service LED flashing) or unit shuts down on airflow
likelyCauses: Broken or slipping belt (belt-drive 6-25 t)
Blower motor overload / bad bearings
Fan proving switch or tubing
VFD fault on VAV / SZVAV units
checks: Belt condition and tension, sheave alignment
Motor amps and bearing noise
Fan proving switch closure with fan running
VFD fault log

commonIssues.symptom: Water in the unit / condensate overflow shutdown
likelyCauses: Clogged condensate drain or trap
Unit not level
Condensate overflow switch tripped (RTOM input)
Missing/incorrect condensate trap for the unit's negative static (blows condensate off the coil)
checks: Clear and flush the drain; verify trap depth against unit negative pressure
Check the overflow switch and reset
Symbio 700: 'High Condensate Level' auto-resets up to two trips in 72 h; the third within 72 h is a Condensate Overflow Lockout needing Reset Diagnostics

commonIssues.symptom: Human Interface shows 'HI COMMUNICATIONS FAILURE' or module communication failures
likelyCauses: IPC link wiring/terminations
Module power loss
Failed module
checks: Inspect the IPC bus wiring at each module and the HI
Check module power LEDs and addresses

commonIssues.symptom: Residential variable-speed heat pump/AC: Err 79.xx low-pressure cut-out (79.00 soft lockout, 79.02 hard lockout)
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge or leak
Restriction (filter drier, EEV, kinked line)
Low indoor airflow in cooling / low outdoor airflow in heating (iced coil, fan)
LPCO switch or wiring fault
checks: LPCO opens at 35 psi / closes at 55 psi in heating; opens at 50 / closes at 70 psi in cooling: compare with measured suction pressure
79.00 = 5 min soft lockout; 79.01 = switch not reset within the soft lockout; 79.02 = hard lockout after multiple trips (cycle power)
Check charge (subcooling charging in Charging Mode-Cooling on Link units), restrictions, indoor/outdoor airflow and LPCO wiring

commonIssues.symptom: Residential variable-speed unit: Err 80.01 high-pressure hard lockout / repeated 'Wait' with reduced capacity (80.00 / 80.02)
likelyCauses: Refrigerant overcharge or non-condensables
Cooling: outdoor fan failure, dirty/blocked outdoor coil, recirculation, very high ambient
Heating: indoor blower failure or indoor airflow restriction
checks: HPCO opens at 650 psig and closes below 500 psig
Each short lockout = 5 min off and capacity reduced by 1/5; 6 short lockouts = 80.01 hard lockout (cycle power); capacity recovers after each 2 h runtime window without a trip
Check outdoor fan and coil (cooling) or blower/filter (heating), then charge

commonIssues.symptom: Residential variable-speed outdoor unit stopped with 184.08 (universal hard lockout)
likelyCauses: A previous hard-lockout alert (e.g. 79.02, 80.01, 177.04, 179.05) - 184.08 follows any hard lockout and drives the outdoor EEV open
checks: Read the alert history in the outdoor Display Assembly (CDA) or thermostat to find the alert that caused it and fix that first
Clear by cycling outdoor power or clearing fault history in the CDA

commonIssues.symptom: Residential variable-speed unit: drive communication fault 176.00 or drive overcurrent 177.0x
likelyCauses: EMI / poor earth ground
AOC-to-drive harness fault (multi-board units)
Outdated AOC/MOC software
Compressor internal short, short to ground or burnt harness at the terminal header (177.04 = 5 hardware or 15 software overcurrents in 1 h)
checks: Power-cycle the outdoor unit and check for solid earth ground; check the AOC to drive harness
Reprogram AOC and MOC to the latest software; call for drive authorization if 176.00 continues
For 177.04 run drive diagnostics / Drive Test (187.01) and follow the Compressor Verification flow chart
Before replacing a drive, call tech support and record the failure mode (warranty claim)

commonIssues.symptom: Residential communicating system: ERR 126.00 EQUIPMENT CHANGE ALERT (Critical) or communication loss
likelyCauses: Power flicker stopped a control from reporting
Equipment replaced or added without rediscovery
Data line (D/B) open, shorted or reversed
checks: Cycle power to each piece of equipment
Measure D to B at the indoor unit: 12-13 VDC normal, about 16 VDC = loss of communication
If equipment was changed, run Restore Factory Defaults to rediscover (resets all settings)
Count amber COMM LED flashes (one per device); rapid flashing = loss of communication

commonIssues.symptom: Residential communicating system: ERR 125.00 low 24 VAC
likelyCauses: Undersized or overloaded transformer
Low line voltage
checks: Measure 24 VAC under load (alert below 24 V)
Transformer sizing for communicating systems: 50 VA with a furnace, 75 VA with an air handler

commonIssues.symptom: Trane/American Standard S-series furnace: ignition lockout 2.1 (retries) or 2.2 (recycles)
likelyCauses: 2.1: gas supply, gas valve, igniter, flame sensor or manifold pressure (flame never proven in 3 tries)
2.2: flame sensed then lost 10 times - dirty flame sensor, poor ground, unstable gas pressure
checks: Both are 1 h lockouts; check L6F fault history first
Manifold about 1.7 in. WC NG / 6.0 in. WC LP (two-stage, 1st stage); max inlet 13.8 in. WC; single-stage S8B1/S8X1 about 3.5 in. WC NG / 10 in. WC LP
Flame current normal 0.75-3 uA DC; below 0.5 uA is bad: clean the sensor and check the ground
Silicon nitride igniter 11-18 ohms cold

commonIssues.symptom: Trane/American Standard S-series furnace: pressure switch codes 3.1-3.4 or code 9 (condensate / inducer limit)
likelyCauses: Blocked vent or intake, tubing off or plugged, inducer fault
Blocked condensate drain or trap
Switch stuck closed or miswired (3.1 / 3.3)
checks: Measure across the switch: 24 V = open, 0 V = closed
Check tubing, vent/intake, inducer; clear the drain and trap

commonIssues.symptom: Trane chiller (CH530 / UC800 / Symbio): diagnostic present, chiller will not restart after reset
likelyCauses: Latching diagnostic needing a local reset (Reset level Local)
Underlying condition still present (NonLatch diagnostics clear only when the condition clears)
Lockout diagnostics (e.g. Compressor Fault Lockout: fault switch open > 35 min or 5 faults in 210 min; Evaporator Water Flow Lost Lockout)
checks: Download active and historic diagnostics with Tracer TU before resetting
Check the Reset level of the diagnostic: 'Local' needs a reset at the chiller (front panel / Tracer TU); 'Remote' can also be reset by the BAS
Look up the diagnostic criteria in the matching chiller platform to find the tripping condition

commonIssues.symptom: Trane BAS controller (Tracer SC / Symbio 800 / UC400 / UC600 / Symbio 400-B/500) not running or not communicating
likelyCauses: No or low 24 VAC (Marquee/Power LED off or solid red)
Reversed polarity on the BACnet MS/TP link (RX LED solid yellow)
Main program crashed repeatedly ('HoLd' on SC / Symbio 800)
Random start delay after power-up (5-30 s on UC400 / Symbio 400-B/500) - normal
checks: Measure 24 VAC at the controller and cycle power
Check link polarity and baud rate
On SC/Symbio 800 read the 7-segment display ('F' + code = fatal, 'H' + code = hardware failure); rotary 999 forces factory defaults
Symbio 400-B/500 firmware recovery: one .scfx file in the USB root, rotaries 991, power up

commonIssues.symptom: Trane WSHP with Symbio 400-B/500 or UC400: Fan Not Energizing
likelyCauses: Unit Wiring: The wiring between the Symbio 400-B/500 controller outputs, fan relays, and contacts must be present and correct for normal fan operation.
Failed End Device: The fan motor and relay must be checked to ensure proper operation.

Normal Operation: The fan turns OFF when: • The Symbio 400-B/500 controller receives a communicated off signal. • The fan-speed switch is set to OFF if no communicated value is present. • Specific diagnostics are generated. • The default fan speed is set to OFF and the fan is operating in the Auto mode. If the Symbio 400-B/500 controller is in unoccupied mode, the fan cycles between OFF and the highest fan speed.

No power to the Controller: If the Symbio 400-B/500 controller does not have power, the unit fan does not operate. For the unit to operate normally, it must have an input voltage of 24 Vac. If the Marquee/Power LED is OFF continuously, the controller does not have sufficient power or has failed.
Diagnostic Present: Several diagnostics affect fan operation.

Unit Configuration: The Symbio 400-B/500 controller must be properly configured based on the actual installed end devices and application. If the unit configuration does not match the actual end device, the fans may not work correctly.
Random Start Observed: After power-up, the Symbio 400-B/500 controller always observes a random start from 5 to 30 seconds. The unit remains OFF until the random start time expires.

Cycling Fan Operation/ Continuous: The Symbio 400-B/500 controller continuously operates the fan when in the occupied, occupied standby, or occupied bypass mode. When the controller is in the unoccupied mode, the fan is cycled between high speed and OFF with capacity.

Unoccupied Operation: Even if the Symbio 400-B/500 controller is configured for continuous fan operation, the fan normally cycles with capacity during unoccupied mode. While unoccupied, the fan cycles ON or OFF with heating/cooling to provide varying amounts of heating or cooling to the space.
Fan Mode Off: If a local fan mode switch determines the fan operation, the OFF position controls the fan to off.

Requested Mode Off: The user can communicate a desired operating mode (such as OFF, heat, and cool) to the controller. If OFF is communicated to the Symbio 400-B/500 controller, it controls the fan to off. There is no heating or cooling.
checks: Unit Wiring: The wiring between the Symbio 400-B/500 controller outputs, fan relays, and contacts must be present and correct for normal fan operation.
Failed End Device: The fan motor and relay must be checked to ensure proper operation.

No power to the Controller: If the Symbio 400-B/500 controller does not have power, the unit fan does not operate. For the unit to operate normally, it must have an input voltage of 24 Vac. If the Marquee/Power LED is OFF continuously, the controller does not have sufficient power or has failed.
Diagnostic Present: Several diagnostics affect fan operation.

Unit Configuration: The Symbio 400-B/500 controller must be properly configured based on the actual installed end devices and application. If the unit configuration does not match the actual end device, the fans may not work correctly.

commonIssues.symptom: Trane WSHP with Symbio 400-B/500 or UC400: Isolation Valves Remain Closed
likelyCauses: Unit Wiring: The wiring between the Symbio 400-B/500 controller outputs and the valve(s) must be present and correct for normal valve operation. Refer to applicable wiring diagram.
Failed End Device: The valves must be checked to ensure proper operation.

No power to the Controller: If the Symbio 400-B/500 controller does not have power, the unit valve(s) will not operate. For the controller to operate normally, apply an input voltage of 24 Vac. If the Marquee/Power LED is OFF continuously, the unit does not have sufficient power or has failed.
Diagnostic Present: Several diagnostics affect valve operation. For detailed information about these diagnostics, refer to Table 13, p. 46.
Normal Operation: The Symbio 400-B/500 controller opens and closes the valves to meet the unit capacity requirements.

Unit Configuration: The Symbio 400-B/500 controller must be properly configured based on the actual installed end devices and application. If the unit configuration does not match the actual end device, the valves may not work correctly.
Random Start Observed: After power-up, the Symbio 400-B/500 controller always observes a random start from 5 to 30 seconds. The controller remains OFF until the random start time expires.

Requested Mode Off: The user can communicate a desired operating mode (such as OFF, heat, and cool) to the Symbio 400-B/500 controller. If OFF is communicated to the unit, the controller controls the fan to off. There is no heating or cooling.

It is used to ensure that the loop water is within appropriate operating temperatures for compressor heating/cooling or valid for waterside economizing. If it is known that sampling is not required, toggling the Entering Water Sampling Enable BV to disabled can be performed.

notes: Web research for this pack was limited to search-engine summaries; WebFetch was unavailable, so the IOM nomenclature pages and the ReliaTel diagnostic tables could not be read in full. Entries marked 'builder memory' or evidence 'inferred' were not re-derived from a document and must be verified before relying on them.

Serial number decoding: 2010+ YYWW, 2002-2009 YWW, 1983-2001 letter+WW — from agreeing secondary decoders (a Trane help-center article on the light-commercial serial date code exists but its digit positions were not read), hence medium. The 1980-1982 style is low; the S/Z letters of 1983-2001 are contested and reported ambiguous (1986 or 2001).
Model nomenclature beyond digit 8 (heating capacity, options) is only partially decoded; read heat input, MCA/MOP and charge from the nameplate.

Refrigerant defaults: R-22 through the early-2000s designs; R-410A on Precedent 3-10 t from 2006 and 12.5-25 t / IntelliPak by 2010; R-454B (A2L) on 2025+ Precedent/Odyssey designs — always confirm from the plate.
Compressor Protection Module (CPM) could not be confirmed as a Trane light-commercial component name; not included.

2026-10-20 extension (from Trane manufacturer PDFs downloaded in phase 2 of the research): residential communicating alerts (System Alert Guide ERR/CFG/SOP and ComfortLink II CL2 lists), variable-speed outdoor IVSC alerts, 4TWZ ComfortLink II outdoor LED codes, furnace IFC codes (S9V2, S9X, S8V2, UHMB/DHMB, R9V), chiller diagnostics (CH530 RTAC / RTWD-RTUD / CGAN-CXAN-CGCL, UCM-CLD, RTWD Series R, RTHD, RTAF, RTZA, RTAG, CGAM, Ascend), Tracer SC / Symbio 800 / UC600 LEDs, WSHP controllers (Symbio 400-B/500, UC400, Axiom basic), SCWM alarms and the Gree-built Trane GMV VRF codes.

Residential: Trane and American Standard share platforms and literature (4TTV/4TWV ~ 4A7V/4A6V, S-series furnaces, AccuLink ~ ComfortLink II); the brand letter is position 2 of outdoor units (T/A) and position 1 of legacy furnaces (T/A).
Trane VRF: the current Trane GMV (TRN-) VRF line is a Gree-built platform (codes are Gree GMV codes); the older Trane/Mitsubishi Electric CITY MULTI line is not covered.

Not covered: CenTraVac (CVHE/CVHF/CVHG/CVHH/CDHF/CDHH) diagnostics (diagnostics manual CTV-SVD005* not public), Agility HDWA diagnostics (not parsed), Link 5TTV/5TWV-specific alert tables (Technical Service Manual 34-4301-01 not obtained), S-series furnace model nomenclature (only a retail-blog key), RTAC/RTAG nomenclature.

Chiller severity in this pack is mapped from the manual's Severity + Persistence (Immediate/Normal + Latch = lockout; + NonLatch = shutdown; Special/Warning = warning; Info = info). Residential System Alert Guide classes map Critical -> shutdown, Major -> warning, Normal -> info.
